﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient﴾

Ḥamzah, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb and al-Aʿmash recited (*Amman*) with a light *mīm*.

The others recited it with a doubled *mīm*. Whoever doubles it has two possible readings:

First: the *mīm* in *ummun* is an added particle (*ṣilah*, a filler), and the sense is interrogative. Its answer is omitted, and the meaning is: "Is one who is devoutly obedient ﴿like one who is not devout﴾?" As in the verse: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam like one whose breast He has not opened?﴾ Or you may say: "Is one who is devoutly obedient like one who has set up rivals to Allah?"

Second: it has the sense of conjunction (*ʿaṭf*) following an interrogative. Its meaning is: "This is better, ﴿or﴾ one who is devoutly obedient," and the answer is omitted because the context indicates it. Many examples of this exist.

Whoever reads it lightly has two possible readings.

First: the *alif* in *Amman* is the vocative particle, with the sense: "O you who are devoutly obedient." The Arabs use the *alif* for addressing just as they use the *yāʾ*, so they say: "Yā Zayd, come" and "Azayd, come."

Aws ibn Ḥajar said:

*"O sons of Labnā, you are not a hand,
a hand without an arm."*

He means: "O sons of Labnā."

Another said:

*"O Aḍmar son of Ḍamrah, what did you mention
of a herd taken at al-Mughār?"*

So the meaning of the verse is: ﴿Say: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed you are among the companions of the Fire."﴾ And: ﴿O you who are devoutly obedient in the watches of the night, indeed you are among the people of Paradise.﴾ As you would say: "So-and-so does not pray or fast," then: "O you who pray and fast, rejoice!" The answer is omitted because the context indicates it.

Second: the *alif* in *Amman* is the interrogative *alif*, and the meaning is: "Is this one like the one who has set up rivals to Allah?" He dispensed with what came before, since the meaning of the speech is clear.

As the poet said:

*"By God, if any thing had come to us from his messenger apart from you,
but we would not find a repelling of it for you."*

He meant: "we would have repelled it."

Ibn ʿUmar said: *al-qunūt* is the recitation of the Qur'an and prolonged standing.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is obedience.

*Ānāʾa al-layl*: its hours. *Sājidan wa-qāʾiman*: prostrating and standing, *yaḥdharu al-ākhirah*: fearing the Hereafter.

﴿And hoping for the mercy of his Lord.﴾

Muqātil said: it was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzūmī.

﴿Say: "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"﴾ — meaning ʿAmmār — ﴿and those who do not know﴾ — meaning Abū Ḥudhayfah. ﴿Only those of understanding are mindful.﴾

al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAdl informed us; Hārūn ibn Muḥammad ibn Hārūn al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us; Ḥāzim ibn Yaḥyā al-Ḥulwānī narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn al-Ṭufayl narrated to us; Hishām ibn Yūsuf narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Yamānī narrated to me, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: Whoever wishes that Allah make the standing (on the Day of Resurrection) easy for him, let him be seen by Allah in the darkness of the night prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord.

﴿Say: "O My servants who believe, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good. And the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account."﴾ Good here means Paradise, according to Muqātil.

al-Suddī said: it means well-being and health.

﴿And the earth of Allah is spacious, so emigrate therein and withdraw from the idols﴾, said Mujāhid.

Muqātil said: it means the land of Paradise.

﴿Indeed the patient will be given their reward without account.﴾

Qatādah said: "No, by God, there is no measure or balance there."

He said: "So may it be, God willing."

﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient﴾

Ḥamzah, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb and al-Aʿmash recited (*Amman*) with a light *mīm*.

The others recited it with a doubled *mīm*. Whoever doubles it has two possible readings:

First: the *mīm* in *ummun* is an added particle (*ṣilah*, a filler), and the sense is interrogative. Its answer is omitted, and the meaning is: "Is one who is devoutly obedient ﴿like one who is not devout﴾?" As in the verse: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam like one whose breast He has not opened?﴾ Or you may say: "Is one who is devoutly obedient like one who has set up rivals to Allah?"

Second: it has the sense of conjunction (*ʿaṭf*) following an interrogative. Its meaning is: "This is better, ﴿or﴾ one who is devoutly obedient," and the answer is omitted because the context indicates it. Many examples of this exist.

Whoever reads it lightly has two possible readings.

First: the *alif* in *Amman* is the vocative particle, with the sense: "O you who are devoutly obedient." The Arabs use the *alif* for addressing just as they use the *yāʾ*, so they say: "Yā Zayd, come" and "Azayd, come."

Aws ibn Ḥajar said:

*"O sons of Labnā, you are not a hand,
a hand without an arm."*

He means: "O sons of Labnā."

Another said:

*"O Aḍmar son of Ḍamrah, what did you mention
of a herd taken at al-Mughār?"*

So the meaning of the verse is: ﴿Say: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed you are among the companions of the Fire."﴾ And: ﴿O you who are devoutly obedient in the watches of the night, indeed you are among the people of Paradise.﴾ As you would say: "So-and-so does not pray or fast," then: "O you who pray and fast, rejoice!" The answer is omitted because the context indicates it.

Second: the *alif* in *Amman* is the interrogative *alif*, and the meaning is: "Is this one like the one who has set up rivals to Allah?" He dispensed with what came before, since the meaning of the speech is clear.

As the poet said:

*"By God, if any thing had come to us from his messenger apart from you,
but we would not find a repelling of it for you."*

He meant: "we would have repelled it."

Ibn ʿUmar said: *al-qunūt* is the recitation of the Qur'an and prolonged standing.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is obedience.

*Ānāʾa al-layl*: its hours. *Sājidan wa-qāʾiman*: prostrating and standing, *yaḥdharu al-ākhirah*: fearing the Hereafter.

﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient﴾

Ḥamzah, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb and al-Aʿmash recited (*Amman*) with a light *mīm*.

The others recited it with a doubled *mīm*. Whoever doubles it has two possible readings:

First: the *mīm* in *ummun* is an added particle (*ṣilah*, a filler), and the sense is interrogative. Its answer is omitted, and the meaning is: "Is one who is devoutly obedient ﴿like one who is not devout﴾?" As in the verse: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam like one whose breast He has not opened?﴾ Or you may say: "Is one who is devoutly obedient like one who has set up rivals to Allah?"

Second: it has the sense of conjunction (*ʿaṭf*) following an interrogative. Its meaning is: "This is better, ﴿or﴾ one who is devoutly obedient," and the answer is omitted because the context indicates it. Many examples of this exist.

Whoever reads it lightly has two possible readings.

First: the *alif* in *Amman* is the vocative particle, with the sense: "O you who are devoutly obedient." The Arabs use the *alif* for addressing just as they use the *yāʾ*, so they say: "Yā Zayd, come" and "Azayd, come."

Aws ibn Ḥajar said:

*"O sons of Labnā, you are not a hand,
a hand without an arm."*

He means: "O sons of Labnā."

Another said:

*"O Aḍmar son of Ḍamrah, what did you mention
of a herd taken at al-Mughār?"*

So the meaning of the verse is: ﴿Say: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed you are among the companions of the Fire."﴾ And: ﴿O you who are devoutly obedient in the watches of the night, indeed you are among the people of Paradise.﴾ As you would say: "So-and-so does not pray or fast," then: "O you who pray and fast, rejoice!" The answer is omitted because the context indicates it.

As the poet said:

*"By God, if any thing had come to us from his messenger apart from you,
but we would not find a repelling of it for you."*

He meant: "we would have repelled it."

Ibn ʿUmar said: *al-qunūt* is the recitation of the Qur'an and prolonged standing.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is obedience.

*Ānāʾa al-layl*: its hours. *Sājidan wa-qāʾiman*: prostrating and standing, *yaḥdharu al-ākhirah*: fearing the Hereafter.

﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient﴾

Ḥamzah, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb and al-Aʿmash recited (*Amman*) with a light *mīm*.

The others recited it with a doubled *mīm*. Whoever doubles it has two possible readings:

First: the *mīm* in *ummun* is an added particle (*ṣilah*, a filler), and the sense is interrogative. Its answer is omitted, and the meaning is: "Is one who is devoutly obedient ﴿like one who is not devout﴾?" As in the verse: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam like one whose breast He has not opened?﴾ Or you may say: "Is one who is devoutly obedient like one who has set up rivals to Allah?"

Second: it has the sense of conjunction (*ʿaṭf*) following an interrogative. Its meaning is: "This is better, ﴿or﴾ one who is devoutly obedient," and the answer is omitted because the context indicates it. Many examples of this exist.

Whoever reads it lightly has two possible readings.

First: the *alif* in *Amman* is the vocative particle, with the sense: "O you who are devoutly obedient." The Arabs use the *alif* for addressing just as they use the *yāʾ*, so they say: "Yā Zayd, come" and "Azayd, come."

Aws ibn Ḥajar said:

*"O sons of Labnā, you are not a hand,
a hand without an arm."*

He means: "O sons of Labnā."

Another said:

*"O Aḍmar son of Ḍamrah, what did you mention
of a herd taken at al-Mughār?"*

So the meaning of the verse is: ﴿Say: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed you are among the companions of the Fire."﴾ And: ﴿O you who are devoutly obedient in the watches of the night, indeed you are among the people of Paradise.﴾ As you would say: "So-and-so does not pray or fast," then: "O you who pray and fast, rejoice!" The answer is omitted because the context indicates it.

Second: the *alif* in *Amman* is the interrogative *alif*, and the meaning is: "Is this one like the one who has set up rivals to Allah?" He dispensed with what came before, since the meaning of the speech is clear.

As the poet said:

*"By God, if any thing had come to us from his messenger apart from you,
but we would not find a repelling of it for you."*

He meant: "we would have repelled it."

Ibn ʿUmar said: *al-qunūt* is the recitation of the Qur'an and prolonged standing.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is obedience.

*Ānāʾa al-layl*: its hours. *Sājidan wa-qāʾiman*: prostrating and standing, *yaḥdharu al-ākhirah*: fearing the Hereafter.

﴿Say: "O My servants who believe, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good. And the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account."﴾ Good here means Paradise, according to Muqātil.

al-Suddī said: it means well-being and health.

﴿And the earth of Allah is spacious, so emigrate therein and withdraw from the idols﴾, said Mujāhid.

Muqātil said: it means the land of Paradise.

Qatādah said: "No, by God, there is no measure or balance there."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed the patient will be given their reward without account﴾, until the people of well-being in this world wish that their bodies were being cut with scissors, because of the excellence the people of affliction receive."

He said: "I have woken up in the blessing of Allah, healthy."

﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient﴾

Ḥamzah, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb and al-Aʿmash recited (*Amman*) with a light *mīm*.

The others recited it with a doubled *mīm*. Whoever doubles it has two possible readings:

First: the *mīm* in *ummun* is an added particle (*ṣilah*, a filler), and the sense is interrogative. Its answer is omitted, and the meaning is: "Is one who is devoutly obedient ﴿like one who is not devout﴾?" As in the verse: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam like one whose breast He has not opened?﴾ Or you may say: "Is one who is devoutly obedient like one who has set up rivals to Allah?"

Second: it has the sense of conjunction (*ʿaṭf*) following an interrogative. Its meaning is: "This is better, ﴿or﴾ one who is devoutly obedient," and the answer is omitted because the context indicates it. Many examples of this exist.

Whoever reads it lightly has two possible readings.

First: the *alif* in *Amman* is the vocative particle, with the sense: "O you who are devoutly obedient." The Arabs use the *alif* for addressing just as they use the *yāʾ*, so they say: "Yā Zayd, come" and "Azayd, come."

Aws ibn Ḥajar said:

*"O sons of Labnā, you are not a hand,
a hand without an arm."*

He means: "O sons of Labnā."

Another said:

*"O Aḍmar son of Ḍamrah, what did you mention
of a herd taken at al-Mughār?"*

So the meaning of the verse is: ﴿Say: "Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed you are among the companions of the Fire."﴾ And: ﴿O you who are devoutly obedient in the watches of the night, indeed you are among the people of Paradise.﴾ As you would say: "So-and-so does not pray or fast," then: "O you who pray and fast, rejoice!" The answer is omitted because the context indicates it.

Second: the *alif* in *Amman* is the interrogative *alif*, and the meaning is: "Is this one like the one who has set up rivals to Allah?" He dispensed with what came before, since the meaning of the speech is clear.

As the poet said:

*"By God, if any thing had come to us from his messenger apart from you,
but we would not find a repelling of it for you."*

He meant: "we would have repelled it."

Ibn ʿUmar said: *al-qunūt* is the recitation of the Qur'an and prolonged standing.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is obedience.

*Ānāʾa al-layl*: its hours. *Sājidan wa-qāʾiman*: prostrating and standing, *yaḥdharu al-ākhirah*: fearing the Hereafter.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid al-WaZZān informed us; Muḥammad ibn Khālid informed us; Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān informed us; ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd informed us; al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us; Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: that he used to recite: (Is one who is devoutly obedient in the watches of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the punishment of the Hereafter).

﴿And hoping for the mercy of his Lord.﴾

Muqātil said: it was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzūmī.

﴿Say: "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"﴾ — meaning ʿAmmār — ﴿and those who do not know﴾ — meaning Abū Ḥudhayfah. ﴿Only those of understanding are mindful.﴾

al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAdl informed us; Hārūn ibn Muḥammad ibn Hārūn al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us; Ḥāzim ibn Yaḥyā al-Ḥulwānī narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn al-Ṭufayl narrated to us; Hishām ibn Yūsuf narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Yamānī narrated to me, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: Whoever wishes that Allah make the standing (on the Day of Resurrection) easy for him, let him be seen by Allah in the darkness of the night prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord.

﴿Say: "O My servants who believe, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good. And the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account."﴾ Good here means Paradise, according to Muqātil.

al-Suddī said: it means well-being and health.

﴿And the earth of Allah is spacious, so emigrate therein and withdraw from the idols﴾, said Mujāhid.

Muqātil said: it means the land of Paradise.

﴿Indeed the patient will be given their reward without account.﴾

Qatādah said: "No, by God, there is no measure or balance there."

al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn Fanjawayh al-Dīnawarī informed us, with my reading to him; Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq al-Sunnī narrated to us; Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated to us; Naṣr ibn Mirzūq narrated to us; Usayd ibn Mūsā narrated to us; Bakr ibn Ḥabīsh narrated to us, from Ḍirār ibn ʿAmr, from Zayd al-Raqqāshī, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The scales will be set up on the Day of Resurrection. The people of prayer will be brought and their rewards given to them by the scales; the people of fasting will be brought and their rewards given to them by the scales; the people of charity will be brought and their rewards given to them by the scales; the people of pilgrimage will be brought and their rewards given to them by the scales; the people of affliction will be brought, and no scale will be set up for them nor any register unrolled for them, and the reward will be poured upon them in a pouring without account. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed the patient will be given their reward without account﴾, until the people of well-being in this world wish that their bodies were being cut with scissors, because of the excellence the people of affliction receive."

He said: Abū ʿAlī ibn Jush al-Muqrī narrated to us: Abū Sahl [from Ismāʿīl ibn Sayf] narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān al-Ḍabaʿī, from Saʿd ibn al-Ṭarīf, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said: I entered with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, to visit him. ʿAlī said to him: "How have you woken up, O son of the Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "I have woken up in the blessing of Allah, healthy."

He said: "So may it be, God willing."

Then al-Ḥasan said: "Support me." ʿAlī supported him against his chest and then said: I heard my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah, say: "O my son, perform the obligations and you will be among the most devout of people; and hold to contentment and you will be the richest of people. O my son, in Paradise there is a tree called the Tree of Trial. The people of affliction will be brought, and no scale will be set up for them nor any register unrolled for them; the reward will be poured upon them in a pouring." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿Indeed the patient will be given their reward without account.﴾

al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Usāmah narrated to us; Dāwūd ibn al-Mukhbir narrated to us; ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr narrated to us, from Abū al-Zinād, from [illegible text] [from Abū Dharr, from the Prophet] that he said: "Whoever is pleased to join those of intellect and understanding, let him endure harm and hardships, for that [illegible text] impatience, and whoever is impatient, his impatience will lead him to the Fire. Nothing attains success on the Day of Resurrection except the patient. Indeed Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed the patient will be given their reward without account﴾, and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate: "Peace be upon you for your patience. How excellent is the final abode."﴾" [Sūrat al-Raʿd: 23–24.] [Abridged in Tafsīr Nūr al-Thaqalayn: 2/501.]

﴿Say: "Indeed I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion. And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims"﴾ from this community. ﴿Say: "Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."﴾ This was when he was called to the religion of his forefathers, according to most of the exegetes.

Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī said: it was abrogated (*mansūkhah*, naskh); the occasion was before the Messenger of Allah's sin was forgiven ((peace be upon him)).

﴿Say: "It is Allah I worship, sincere to Him in my religion. So worship what you will besides Him."﴾

This is a command of rebuke and threat, like His saying: ﴿Do what you will.﴾ It was said: it was abrogated by the verse of fighting. ﴿Say: "Indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves, their families, their spouses and their servants on the Day of Resurrection. Is that not the clear loss?"﴾

Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah the Exalted has made for every person a dwelling and family in Paradise. Whoever acts in obedience to Allah the Exalted will have that dwelling and family; and whoever acts in disobedience to Allah, Allah the Exalted takes him to the Fire, and the dwelling becomes an inheritance for whoever acted in obedience to Allah, in addition to what was his before. This is His saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors.﴾

﴿For them there will be canopies of Fire above them and canopies beneath them.﴾ Canopies (*ẓulal*): layers and enclosures of Fire and its smoke, and beneath them canopies: a bed and couch of Fire. The lower layer was called a canopy only because it is a canopy over those beneath them. Its like is His saying: ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and above them are coverings﴾, and His saying: ﴿The Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾, and His saying: ﴿Its enclosure surrounds them﴾, and His saying: ﴿And a shade of black smoke﴾, and His glorified and exalted saying: ﴿Proceed to a shade of three branches.﴾

﴿That is what Allah makes His servants fear. O My servants, fear Me. And those who avoid the *ṭāghūt* (the idols), that they not worship them, and turn back in repentance to Allah, for them there is good news. So give good tidings to My servants, who listen to the word and follow the best of it.﴾ Turn back (*anābū*): returned to Allah, to the worship of Allah. For them is good news (*al-bushrā*) in this world of Paradise and in the Hereafter. ﴿Give good tidings to My servants who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾: guided and directed to the truth.

As the poet said:

*"By God, if any thing had come to us from his messenger apart from you,
but we would not find a repelling of it for you."*

He meant: "we would have repelled it."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is obedience.

﴿And hoping for the mercy of his Lord.﴾

Muqātil said: it was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Makhzūmī.

﴿Say: "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"﴾ — meaning ʿAmmār — ﴿and those who do not know﴾ — meaning Abū Ḥudhayfah. ﴿Only those of understanding are mindful.﴾

al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAdl informed us; Hārūn ibn Muḥammad ibn Hārūn al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us; Ḥāzim ibn Yaḥyā al-Ḥulwānī narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn al-Ṭufayl narrated to us; Hishām ibn Yūsuf narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Yamānī narrated to me, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: Whoever wishes that Allah make the standing (on the Day of Resurrection) easy for him, let him be seen by Allah in the darkness of the night prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord.

﴿Say: "O My servants who believe, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good. And the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account."﴾ Good here means Paradise, according to Muqātil.

al-Suddī said: it means well-being and health.

﴿And the earth of Allah is spacious, so emigrate therein and withdraw from the idols﴾, said Mujāhid.

Muqātil said: it means the land of Paradise.

﴿Indeed the patient will be given their reward without account.﴾

Qatādah said: "No, by God, there is no measure or balance there."

The people of prayer will be brought and their rewards given to them by the scales; the people of fasting will be brought and their rewards given to them by the scales; the people of charity will be brought and their rewards given to them by the scales; the people of pilgrimage will be brought and their rewards given to them by the scales; the people of affliction will be brought, and no scale will be set up for them nor any register unrolled for them, and the reward will be poured upon them in a pouring without account. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed the patient will be given their reward without account﴾, until the people of well-being in this world wish that their bodies were being cut with scissors, because of the excellence the people of affliction receive."

He said: Abū ʿAlī ibn Jush al-Muqrī narrated to us: Abū Sahl [from Ismāʿīl ibn Sayf] narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān al-Ḍabaʿī, from Saʿd ibn al-Ṭarīf, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said: I entered with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, to visit him. ʿAlī said to him: "How have you woken up, O son of the Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "I have woken up in the blessing of Allah, healthy."

He said: "So may it be, God willing."

Then al-Ḥasan said: "Support me." ʿAlī supported him against his chest and then said: I heard my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah, say: "O my son, perform the obligations and you will be among the most devout of people; and hold to contentment and you will be the richest of people. O my son, in Paradise there is a tree called the Tree of Trial. The people of affliction will be brought, and no scale will be set up for them nor any register unrolled for them; the reward will be poured upon them in a pouring." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿Indeed the patient will be given their reward without account.﴾

al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Usāmah narrated to us; Dāwūd ibn al-Mukhbir narrated to us; ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr narrated to us, from Abū al-Zinād, from [illegible text] [from Abū Dharr, from the Prophet] that he said: "Whoever is pleased to join those of intellect and understanding, let him endure harm and hardships, for that [illegible text] impatience, and whoever is impatient, his impatience will lead him to the Fire. This is a command of rebuke and threat, like His saying: ﴿Do what you will.﴾ It was said: it was abrogated by the verse of fighting. ﴿Say: "Indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves, their families, their spouses and their servants on the Day of Resurrection. And the like of this is abundant.

﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient﴾

Ḥamzah, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb and al-Aʿmash recited (*Amman*) with a light *mīm*.

The others recited it with a doubled *mīm*. Whoever doubles it has two possible readings:

First: the *mīm* in *ummun* is an added particle (*ṣilah*, a filler), and the sense is interrogative. Its answer is omitted, and the meaning is: "Is one who is devoutly obedient ﴿like one who is not devout﴾?" As in the verse: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam like one whose breast He has not opened?﴾ Or you may say: "Is one who is devoutly obedient like one who has set up rivals to Allah?"

Second: it has the sense of conjunction (*ʿaṭf*) following an interrogative. Its meaning is: "This is better, ﴿or﴾ one who is devoutly obedient," and the answer is omitted because the context indicates it. Many examples of this exist.

Whoever reads it lightly has two possible readings.

First: the *alif* in *Amman* is the vocative particle, with the sense: "O you who are devoutly obedient." The Arabs use the *alif* for addressing just as they use the *yāʾ*, so they say: "Yā Zayd, come" and "Azayd, come."

Aws ibn Ḥajar said:

a hand without an arm."*

He means: "O sons of Labnā."

of a herd taken at al-Mughār?"*

For those who have feared their Lord, there are chambers (ghuraf) built high, with rivers flowing beneath them—Allah's promise; Allah does not fail in His promise. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they are of chrysolite and ruby. [Source: the preceding work.]

Al-Tha'alabi, Ṭabaqat... Sorry, the passage is: [Chain] ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, [ ... ] (unreadable text) related to us Talha, who related to us Hammad, from Abu Harun, from Malik ibn Anas, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise will look upon the people of the chambers above them as you look upon the bright star that glimmers on the horizon in the east or the west, because of the excellence between them." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, those are the dwellings of the prophets, which none other than they can reach." He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand my soul is, they are men who believed in Allah and affirmed the messengers." [Source: Tafsir al-Qurtubi 13/359; similar in Sahih al-Bukhari 4/88 and Sahih Muslim 8/145.]

Rivers flow beneath them—Allah's promise (waʿda Allah), accusative as an infinitive (maṣdar). Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, i.e., from the clouds, and makes it enter springs (yanabi', springs) in the earth? Al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak said: all water in the earth descends from the sky; it descends from the sky to the rock, then from it He divides springs and wells. Then He brings forth by it crops of varying colours; then it dries up (yahij) and you see it turn yellow after its greenness; then He makes it debris (hutaman), i.e., broken and crumbling bits. Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding.

Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam (lil-islam, to faith), so that he is upon light from his Lord—? Qatada said: the light is the Book of Allah; from it you take and to it we return. [Source: Fath al-Qadir 4/458.] The meaning of the verse: "Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam, and who is upon light from his Lord, [equal to one whose heart is hardened]? That is, is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam like one whose heart is hardened?"

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Fanjawayh related to us, ʿUbayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba related to us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Yazid related to us, al-Mawsili related to us in Baghdad, Abu Farwa, whose name is Yazid ibn Muhammad, related to us, my father related to me, from his father, Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah has opened his breast to Islam, he is upon light from his Lord."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is the opening of his breast?"

He said: "When the light enters the heart, it opens and expands."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the sign of that?"

He said: "Turning penitently to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before death comes."

Al-Tha'labi said: We have been informed that it was revealed concerning ʿAmmar ibn Yasir. Al-Tha'labi said: We have been informed that it was revealed concerning ʿAmmar ibn Yasir. [See Tafsir Abi Hamza: 287; al-Qurtubi said: what is meant by "whose breast Allah has opened" here, according to what the exegetes mentioned, is ʿAli and Hamza.] Muqatil said: "Whose breast Allah has opened to Islam" refers to the Prophet (ﷺ).

So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Abu Jahl and his kin among the disbelievers. Those are in manifest error.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Hafiz related to us, Abu Ahmad al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Rabbih al-Sarraj al-Sufi related to us, [ ... ] (unreadable word), Yunus ibn Ya'qub al-Bazzaz related to us, al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Samh al-Basri related to us in Baghdad, Jandal related to us, Abu Malik al-Wasiti al-Husayni related to us, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Nadra, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Seek your needs from the generous-hearted, for I have placed My mercy in them; and do not seek them from those whose hearts are hard, for I have placed My wrath in them." [Source: Tafsir al-Qurtubi 15/248.]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ibrahim ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us from Wahb, Yusuf ibn al-Sabbah al-ʿAttar related to us, Ibrahim ibn Sulayman ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, my paternal uncle Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, Yusuf ibn Maysara ibn Jubayr related to us, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is Gentle and loves gentleness in all matters, and He loves every humble, forbearing, merciful heart that teaches people good and calls to obedience to Allah, and He hates every hard heart that sleeps all night without remembering Allah, the Exalted, and does not know whether its spirit will be returned to it or not." [Source: Kanz al-ʿUmmal 3/39, no. 5370.]

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Fanjawayh related to us, Ibn Nasrawayh related to us, Ibn Wahb related to us, Ibrahim ibn Bistam related to us, Sa'id ibn ʿAmir related to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Malik ibn Dinar, who said: No servant has been struck with a punishment greater than the hardness of his heart, and Allah has not become angry with a people without removing mercy from them.

Allah has sent down the best of speech, a Book, consistent with itself (mutashabihan).

Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn ʿAbbas said: The Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would tell us," and then it was revealed: Allah has sent down the best of speech, a Book, consistent with itself (mutashabihan), some of it resembling other parts in beauty, confirming one another, with no contradiction or discrepancy in it. [See Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/249.]

Qatada said: Verses resemble verses, words resemble words, and letters resemble letters.

Oft-repeated (mathani) — the Qur'an. The exegetes said: the Qur'an is called mathani because reports, rulings, and limits are repeated in it, and it is repeated in recitation, so it never becomes tiresome. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver; then their skins and hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah.

That is, to acting upon the Book of Allah and affirming it. It was also said that "ila" here means "li" (for/to).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh related to us, ʿUbayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, Ahmad ibn Dawud related to us, Salama ibn Shabib related to us, Khalaf ibn Salama related to us from him, Hushaym related to us, from Husayn, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, who said: I said to my grandmother Asma' bint Abi Bakr: How did the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) behave when the Qur'an was recited to them?

She said: They were as Allah described them: their eyes would weep and their skins would shiver.

I said to her: Today some people, when the Qur'an is recited to them—

She said: They are as He described them: one of them falls down unconscious.

Then she said: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

And through him, from Salama: Yahya ibn Yahya related to us, Sa'id ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Jumahi related to us: that Ibn ʿUmar passed by a man from Iraq who had collapsed, and said: "What is wrong with this one?"

They said: "When the Qur'an is recited to him and he hears the remembrance of Allah, he collapses."

Ibn ʿUmar said: "Indeed we fear Allah, yet we do not collapse."

Ibn ʿUmar also said: "Indeed Satan enters into the belly of one of them. This was not the practice of the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh related to us, Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Husayn ibn [Dizil] related to us, Abu Nu'aym related to us, ʿImran or Humran ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz related to us, who said: Those who fall unconscious when the Qur'an is recited were mentioned in the presence of Ibn Sirin, and he said: "Between us and them is this: one of them should sit on the roof of a house with his legs outstretched, and the Qur'an be recited to him from beginning to end. If he throws himself down, then he is truthful." [Source: Tafsir al-Qurtubi 15/249.]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us, Abu Bakr ibn Malik related to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, Salt ibn Mas'ud al-Jahdari related to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, Abu ʿImran al-Jawni related to us, who said: Musa (peace be upon him) admonished his people, and a man among them tore his shirt. It was said to Musa: "Tell the owner of the shirt: do not tear your shirt; will his heart be opened to me?"

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Samura al-Baghawi related to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Shayba related to us, al-Hasan ibn Sa'id ibn ʿUmar related to us, Sa'dan ibn Nasr Abu ʿAli related to us, [Nashaba], from Abu Ghassan al-Madani Muhammad ibn Mutarrif, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), and [the people] wept. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seize the opportunity to supplicate at the time of tenderness, for it is a mercy." [Source: Musnad al-Shihab of Ibn Salama 1/402; Kanz al-ʿUmmal 2/102, no. 3341.]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Barza and Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Marwazi related to us, Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Hammani related to us, Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, and Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli related to us, Muhammad ibn ʿAbduws ibn Kamil related to us, Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Hammani related to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad related to us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Umm Kulthum bint al-ʿAbbas, from al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"When the skin of a servant shivers from fear of Allah, his sins fall away from him as the withered leaves fall from a dry tree." [Source: Majma' al-Zawa'id 10/310; Kanz al-ʿUmmal 3/141, no. 5879, where it reads: "the withered leaves."]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, Ahmad ibn Ja'far related to us, Hamdan related to us, Musa ibn Ishaq al-Ansari related to us, Muhammad ibn Ma'una related to us, al-Layth ibn Sa'd related to us, Yazid ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Had related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Umm Kulthum bint al-ʿAbbas, from her father, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "When the skin of a servant shivers from fear of Allah, Allah forbids him to the Fire." [Source: 130.]

That, i.e., the best speech, is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whom He wills, and whom Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide. This contains a refutation of the Qadariyya.

Is one who shields with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection—? That is, its severity on the Day of Resurrection.

Mujahid said: He will be dragged on his face in the Fire.

ʿAta' said: He will be cast into the Fire upside down, so the first thing the Fire touches is his face.

Muqatil said: It is that the disbeliever is cast into the Fire with his hands chained to his neck, and on his neck is a huge rock like a great mountain of sulphur. The fire ignites the stone while it hangs from his neck, and its heat and blaze strike his face, and he cannot push it away from his face because of the shackles on his hands and neck. The meaning of the verse: "Is one who shields with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection" is like one who is secure from the punishment. It is like His saying: "Is one who is cast into the Fire better...?" [Fussilat 40].

Al-Musayyab said: This verse was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.

It is said (wa-qila), that is, the keepers will say to the wrongdoers: "Taste what you used to earn," that is, its consequence. Those before them denied, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive. So Allah made them taste the disgrace (khizy), the punishment and humiliation that is shameful, in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew. And We have certainly struck for people in this Qur'an every kind of example, that they may remember. [It is] an Arabic Qur'an, accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), without crookedness (ghayra dhi ʿiwaj).

Mujahid said: That is, without doubt (ghayra dhi labs).

ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan said: without contradiction (ghayr mutadadd).

Ibn ʿAbbas: without disagreement (ghayr mukhtalif).

Al-Suddi: uncreated (ghayr makhluq).

Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani: without error in grammar (ghayr dhi laḥn).

So that they may be wary (la'allahum yattaqun) of disbelief and denying it.

﴿Allah has struck a parable: a man﴾.

Al-Kisa'i said: "رَجُلًا" (rajulan, "a man") is in the accusative because it is an explanation (tarjamah) of the parable (mathal) and an elaboration of it. If you wish, it can be read in the accusative by omitting the preposition, so that the sense is "Allah has struck a parable for a man, or concerning a man."

﴿In it are partners in dispute (mutashakisun)﴾: disagreeing, quarrelling, contending with one another over it, each one of them making him serve according to his share in it. It is said: "rajul shaks," "shiras," "dhiras," and "dabs," when a man is of bad character and opposed to people.

The philologist (al-Mu'arrikh) said: "mutashakisun" means "mutamaksun" (bargaining with one another). It is said: "shakasani fulan," meaning "makasani fulan" (he haggled with me).

﴿And a man wholly (salaman) belonging to one man﴾.

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub read "سالما" (saliman) with an alif. Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading, saying: "We have chosen 'saliman' because the interpretation of it is sound, for the 'salim' is the pure, unmixed one, which is the opposite of the shared (mushtarak). As for 'salm,' it is the opposite of the warrior, and there is no place for war here."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "سِلْماً" (silman) with a kasrah on the sin and a sukun on the lam.

The rest read "سَلَماً" (salaman) with a fatha on the sin and the lam, without an alif. Abu Hatim chose this reading and said: "It is that over which there is no dispute."

﴿Are the two equal in comparison?﴾ This is a parable Allah struck for the disbeliever who worships many gods, and for the believer who worships none but the One God. Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Praise be to Allah﴾, meaning complete thanks belong to Allah, the Glorified, apart from every other object of worship. ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ ﴿Indeed you, O Muhammad, are dying (mayyit) before long, and indeed they are dying (mayyitun).﴾

Ibn Muhayşin and Ibn Abi 'Ilyah read: "إنك مايت وإنهم مايتون" (innaka mayit wa innahum mayitun), with an alif in both.

Al-Hasan, al-Kisa'i, and al-Farra' said: "al-mayyit," with tashdid, is one who has not yet died but will die. "al-mayt," with takhfif, is one whose soul has departed. Therefore it is not lightened here.

Qatada said: The death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced to him, and your deaths were announced to you.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Majah narrated to us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us: Sayyar ibn Hatim narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Thabit said: A man's brother's death was announced to Salt ibn Ushaym, but he found him eating. He said: "Come near and eat, for my brother's death was announced to me some time ago."

He said: "How? I was the first to bring you the news." He said: "Allah the Exalted announced it to me, saying:" ﴿Indeed you are dying, and indeed they are dying﴾.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/254. The addition in the brackets is from it.]]

﴿Then indeed on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute with one another.﴾ That is, the righteous and the wrongdoer, the oppressor and the oppressed.

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Ibn Malik narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib, from Abd Allah ibn Anas, from al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, who said: When there was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ﴿Then indeed on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute with one another﴾,

al-Zubayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will what was between us in this world be repeated to us, along with the particular sins?"

He said: "Yes, it will certainly be repeated upon you, until every person with a right is given his right."

Al-Zubayr said: "By Allah, the matter is indeed severe."[[Musnad Ahmad: 1/167; al-Mustadrak: 2/435.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn Abd Allah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn al-Husayn ibn [Dizil] narrated to us: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us: Sa'id al-Muqri' narrated to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever has an injustice against his brother concerning his wealth or his honour, let him seek his pardon for it today, before there comes a time when there is no dinar or dirham. If he has good deeds, they will be taken from him in proportion to his injustice; and if he has no good deeds, the bad deeds of his companion will be taken and placed upon him."[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/506; Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/99.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Abi Bakr al-Burjumi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Minhal narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Rawh ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you know who is bankrupt (muflis) among my community?"

We said: "Yes, the one who has no wealth."

He said: "No. The bankrupt of my community is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection having struck this one, reviled that one, and taken the wealth of this one. So his good deeds are taken and placed on the good deeds of the other. If his good deeds are exhausted before his debts are paid, the bad deeds of the other are taken and cast upon him. Then he is taken and thrown into the Fire."[[133]]

Abu al-'Aliyah said: They are the people of the qiblah (those who face the Ka'bah in prayer).

Al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyyah narrated to us: Ubayd ibn Junad al-'Alawi al-Halabi narrated to us: Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from al-Qasim ibn 'Awf al-Bakri, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: "We lived a span of our lives thinking that this verse was revealed concerning us and the People of the Two Books: ﴿Then indeed on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute with one another﴾. We said: 'How will we dispute, when our Prophet is one and our Book is one? What is this dispute?' Until I saw some of us striking the faces of others with swords, and I knew that it was revealed concerning us."

Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, concerning this verse, that he said: "We used to say: 'Our Lord is one, our religion is one, and our Prophet is one. What is this dispute?' When it was the day of Siffin and some of us attacked others with swords, we said: 'Yes, this is it.'"

Al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi narrated to us: Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Ibn 'Awn claimed, from Ibrahim, who said:

When there was revealed ﴿Then indeed on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute with one another﴾, they said: "How will we dispute, when we are brothers?" Then when 'Uthman was killed, they said: "This is our dispute."

﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies against Allah, claiming that He has a son and a partner, and denies the truth (al-sidq), that is, the Qur'an, when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling (mathwa), a place of residence, for the disbelievers? And he who brought the truth and affirmed it﴾.

Al-Suddi said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" means Jibril, who brought the Qur'an. "﴿And affirmed it﴾" means Muhammad, who received it with acceptance.

Ibn Abbas said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" means the Messenger of Allah, who brought "There is no god but Allah." "﴿And affirmed it﴾" is also the Messenger of Allah, who conveyed it to creation.

Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu al-'Aliyah, and al-Kalbi said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" means the Messenger of Allah, and "﴿affirmed it﴾" means Abu Bakr.

Qatada and Muqatil said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" is the Messenger of Allah, and "﴿affirmed it﴾" refers to the believers, and they cited His saying: ﴿Those are the God-fearing (al-muttaqun)﴾.

'Ata' said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" refers to the Prophets (peace be upon them), and "﴿affirmed it﴾" refers to their followers. In this case "alladhi" (the one who) is in the sense of "alladhina" (those who) by way of the generic category, as in His saying: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire﴾,[[Surah al-Baqarah: 17.]] then He said: ﴿Allah took away their light﴾,[[Surah al-Baqarah: 17.]] and His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe﴾.[[Surah al-'Asr: 2.]]

The evidence for this interpretation is what Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Talhah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Mujahid: Abdan ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to us: Ammar ibn al-Hasan narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': that he used to read "والذين جاؤ" (wa'l-ladhina ja'u), meaning the Prophets (peace be upon them), "وصدقوا به" (wa saddaqu bihi), meaning their followers.

Al-Hasan said: "He is the believer who affirmed it in this world and will bring it on the Day of Resurrection."

This is supported by what Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu 'Ali ibn Habash al-Muqri' informed us, [saying]: al-Zahrani (yaʿni al-Zuhrani) informed us: Yahya ibn al-Fadl al-Kharqi narrated to us: Wuhayb ibn 'Amr narrated to us: Harun al-Nahwi informed us, from Muhammad ibn Hujarah, from Abu Salih al-Kufi, who is Abu Salih al-Sammān, that he read "وَالَّذِي جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ" with the lightened form (takhfif), and said: "He is the believer who brought it truthfully and affirmed it."

Mujahid said: "They are the people of the Qur'an, who will come with it on the Day of Resurrection saying: 'This is what you gave us, and we acted upon what is in it.'"

﴿Those are the God-fearing. For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the good-doers. That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did, and reward them with their best deeds.﴾ ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾

Abu Ja'far, Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read "عباده" (ibadahu), in the plural.

The rest read "عَبْدَهُ" (abdahu), meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

﴿And they frighten you with those other than Him.﴾ This was because they frightened the Prophet ﷺ with the harm of the idols and said: "You are denigrating our gods and speaking of them evilly. By Allah, either you desist from mentioning them, or we will forsake you, or they will afflict you with harm."

﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide. And whomever Allah guides, for him there is no misleader. Is not Allah Mighty, Able to Take Vengeance?﴾ ﴿And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah.' Say: 'Have you considered what you invoke other than Allah? If Allah should intend for me some harm (durr), that is, hardship and affliction, can they remove His harm? Or if He should intend for me mercy (rahmah), that is, blessing and ease, can they withhold His mercy?'﴾

Shaybah, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub read both "ضُرِّهِ" and "رَحْمَتِهِ" with tanwin (kashifatun, mumsikatun, unindefinite), and this was chosen by Abu 'Ubaydah and Abu Hatim.

The rest read them with the idafah (genitive construction).

Muqatil said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) asked them, and they were silent. So Allah the Glorified sent down: ﴿Say: "Allah is sufficient for me; in Him the trusting trust."﴾ ﴿Say: "O my people, act according to your standing; indeed I am acting, so you will come to know, when there comes upon you a punishment (ba's) from Allah."﴾ That is, who among us is in the right and who is in the wrong.

﴿Allah has struck a parable: a man﴾.

Al-Kisa'i said: "رَجُلًا" (rajulan, "a man") is in the accusative because it is an explanation (tarjamah) of the parable (mathal) and an elaboration of it. If you wish, it can be read in the accusative by omitting the preposition, so that the sense is "Allah has struck a parable for a man, or concerning a man."

﴿In it are partners in dispute (mutashakisun)﴾: disagreeing, quarrelling, contending with one another over it, each one of them making him serve according to his share in it. It is said: "rajul shaks," "shiras," "dhiras," and "dabs," when a man is of bad character and opposed to people.

The philologist (al-Mu'arrikh) said: "mutashakisun" means "mutamaksun" (bargaining with one another). It is said: "shakasani fulan," meaning "makasani fulan" (he haggled with me).

﴿And a man wholly (salaman) belonging to one man﴾.

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub read "سالما" (saliman) with an alif. Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading, saying: "We have chosen 'saliman' because the interpretation of it is sound, for the 'salim' is the pure, unmixed one, which is the opposite of the shared (mushtarak). As for 'salm,' it is the opposite of the warrior, and there is no place for war here."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "سِلْماً" (silman) with a kasrah on the sin and a sukun on the lam.

The rest read "سَلَماً" (salaman) with a fatha on the sin and the lam, without an alif. Abu Hatim chose this reading and said: "It is that over which there is no dispute."

﴿Are the two equal in comparison?﴾ This is a parable Allah struck for the disbeliever who worships many gods, and for the believer who worships none but the One God. Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Praise be to Allah﴾, meaning complete thanks belong to Allah, the Glorified, apart from every other object of worship. ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ ﴿Indeed you, O Muhammad, are dying (mayyit) before long, and indeed they are dying (mayyitun).﴾

Ibn Muhayşin and Ibn Abi 'Ilyah read: "إنك مايت وإنهم مايتون" (innaka mayit wa innahum mayitun), with an alif in both.

Al-Hasan, al-Kisa'i, and al-Farra' said: "al-mayyit," with tashdid, is one who has not yet died but will die. "al-mayt," with takhfif, is one whose soul has departed. Therefore it is not lightened here.

Qatada said: The death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced to him, and your deaths were announced to you.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Majah narrated to us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us: Sayyar ibn Hatim narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Thabit said: A man's brother's death was announced to Salt ibn Ushaym, but he found him eating. He said: "Come near and eat, for my brother's death was announced to me some time ago."

He said: "How? I was the first to bring you the news." He said: "Allah the Exalted announced it to me, saying:" ﴿Indeed you are dying, and indeed they are dying﴾.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/254. The addition in the brackets is from it.]]

﴿Then indeed on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute with one another.﴾ That is, the righteous and the wrongdoer, the oppressor and the oppressed.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Abi Bakr al-Burjumi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Minhal narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Rawh ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you know who is bankrupt (muflis) among my community?"

We said: "Yes, the one who has no wealth."

He said: "No. The bankrupt of my community is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection having struck this one, reviled that one, and taken the wealth of this one. So his good deeds are taken and placed on the good deeds of the other. If his good deeds are exhausted before his debts are paid, the bad deeds of the other are taken and cast upon him. Then he is taken and thrown into the Fire."[[133]]

Abu al-'Aliyah said: They are the people of the qiblah (those who face the Ka'bah in prayer).

Al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Alawiyyah narrated to us: Ubayd ibn Junad al-'Alawi al-Halabi narrated to us: Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from al-Qasim ibn 'Awf al-Bakri, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: "We lived a span of our lives thinking that this verse was revealed concerning us and the People of the Two Books: ﴿Then indeed on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute with one another﴾. We said: 'How will we dispute, when our Prophet is one and our Book is one? What is this dispute?' Until I saw some of us striking the faces of others with swords, and I knew that it was revealed concerning us."

Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, concerning this verse, that he said: "We used to say: 'Our Lord is one, our religion is one, and our Prophet is one. What is this dispute?' When it was the day of Siffin and some of us attacked others with swords, we said: 'Yes, this is it.'"

Al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi narrated to us: Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Ibn 'Awn claimed, from Ibrahim, who said:

When there was revealed ﴿Then indeed on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute with one another﴾, they said: "How will we dispute, when we are brothers?" Then when 'Uthman was killed, they said: "This is our dispute."

﴿So who is more unjust than one who lies against Allah, claiming that He has a son and a partner, and denies the truth (al-sidq), that is, the Qur'an, when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling (mathwa), a place of residence, for the disbelievers? And he who brought the truth and affirmed it﴾.

Al-Suddi said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" means Jibril, who brought the Qur'an. "﴿And affirmed it﴾" means Muhammad, who received it with acceptance.

Ibn Abbas said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" means the Messenger of Allah, who brought "There is no god but Allah." "﴿And affirmed it﴾" is also the Messenger of Allah, who conveyed it to creation.

Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu al-'Aliyah, and al-Kalbi said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" means the Messenger of Allah, and "﴿affirmed it﴾" means Abu Bakr.

Qatada and Muqatil said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" is the Messenger of Allah, and "﴿affirmed it﴾" refers to the believers, and they cited His saying: ﴿Those are the God-fearing (al-muttaqun)﴾.

'Ata' said: "﴿He who brought the truth﴾" refers to the Prophets (peace be upon them), and "﴿affirmed it﴾" refers to their followers. In this case "alladhi" (the one who) is in the sense of "alladhina" (those who) by way of the generic category, as in His saying: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire﴾,[[Surah al-Baqarah: 17.]] then He said: ﴿Allah took away their light﴾,[[Surah al-Baqarah: 17.]] and His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe﴾.[[Surah al-'Asr: 2.]]

The evidence for this interpretation is what Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Talhah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Mujahid: Abdan ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to us: Ammar ibn al-Hasan narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': that he used to read "والذين جاؤ" (wa'l-ladhina ja'u), meaning the Prophets (peace be upon them), "وصدقوا به" (wa saddaqu bihi), meaning their followers.

Al-Hasan said: "He is the believer who affirmed it in this world and will bring it on the Day of Resurrection."

This is supported by what Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu 'Ali ibn Habash al-Muqri' informed us, [saying]: al-Zahrani (yaʿni al-Zuhrani) informed us: Yahya ibn al-Fadl al-Kharqi narrated to us: Wuhayb ibn 'Amr narrated to us: Harun al-Nahwi informed us, from Muhammad ibn Hujarah, from Abu Salih al-Kufi, who is Abu Salih al-Sammān, that he read "وَالَّذِي جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ" with the lightened form (takhfif), and said: "He is the believer who brought it truthfully and affirmed it."

Mujahid said: "They are the people of the Qur'an, who will come with it on the Day of Resurrection saying: 'This is what you gave us, and we acted upon what is in it.'"

﴿Those are the God-fearing. For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the good-doers. That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did, and reward them with their best deeds.﴾ ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾

Abu Ja'far, Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read "عباده" (ibadahu), in the plural.

The rest read "عَبْدَهُ" (abdahu), meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

﴿And they frighten you with those other than Him.﴾ This was because they frightened the Prophet ﷺ with the harm of the idols and said: "You are denigrating our gods and speaking of them evilly. By Allah, either you desist from mentioning them, or we will forsake you, or they will afflict you with harm."

﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide. And whomever Allah guides, for him there is no misleader. Is not Allah Mighty, Able to Take Vengeance?﴾ ﴿And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah.' Say: 'Have you considered what you invoke other than Allah? If Allah should intend for me some harm (durr), that is, hardship and affliction, can they remove His harm? Or if He should intend for me mercy (rahmah), that is, blessing and ease, can they withhold His mercy?'﴾

Shaybah, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub read both "ضُرِّهِ" and "رَحْمَتِهِ" with tanwin (kashifatun, mumsikatun, unindefinite), and this was chosen by Abu 'Ubaydah and Abu Hatim.

The rest read them with the idafah (genitive construction).

Muqatil said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) asked them, and they were silent. So Allah the Glorified sent down: ﴿Say: "Allah is sufficient for me; in Him the trusting trust."﴾ ﴿Say: "O my people, act according to your standing; indeed I am acting, so you will come to know, when there comes upon you a punishment (ba's) from Allah."﴾ That is, who among us is in the right and who is in the wrong.

﴿Allah has struck a parable: a man﴾.

Al-Kisa'i said: "رَجُلًا" (rajulan, "a man") is in the accusative because it is an explanation (tarjamah) of the parable (mathal) and an elaboration of it. If you wish, it can be read in the accusative by omitting the preposition, so that the sense is "Allah has struck a parable for a man, or concerning a man."

﴿In it are partners in dispute (mutashakisun)﴾: disagreeing, quarrelling, contending with one another over it, each one of them making him serve according to his share in it. It is said: "rajul shaks," "shiras," "dhiras," and "dabs," when a man is of bad character and opposed to people.

The philologist (al-Mu'arrikh) said: "mutashakisun" means "mutamaksun" (bargaining with one another). It is said: "shakasani fulan," meaning "makasani fulan" (he haggled with me).

﴿And a man wholly (salaman) belonging to one man﴾.

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub read "سالما" (saliman) with an alif. Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading, saying: "We have chosen 'saliman' because the interpretation of it is sound, for the 'salim' is the pure, unmixed one, which is the opposite of the shared (mushtarak). As for 'salm,' it is the opposite of the warrior, and there is no place for war here."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "سِلْماً" (silman) with a kasrah on the sin and a sukun on the lam.

The rest read "سَلَماً" (salaman) with a fatha on the sin and the lam, without an alif. Abu Hatim chose this reading and said: "It is that over which there is no dispute."

﴿Are the two equal in comparison?﴾ This is a parable Allah struck for the disbeliever who worships many gods, and for the believer who worships none but the One God. Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Praise be to Allah﴾, meaning complete thanks belong to Allah, the Glorified, apart from every other object of worship. ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ ﴿Indeed you, O Muhammad, are dying (mayyit) before long, and indeed they are dying (mayyitun).﴾

Ibn Muhayşin and Ibn Abi 'Ilyah read: "إنك مايت وإنهم مايتون" (innaka mayit wa innahum mayitun), with an alif in both.

Al-Hasan, al-Kisa'i, and al-Farra' said: "al-mayyit," with tashdid, is one who has not yet died but will die. "al-mayt," with takhfif, is one whose soul has departed. Therefore it is not lightened here.

Qatada said: The death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced to him, and your deaths were announced to you.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Majah narrated to us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us: Sayyar ibn Hatim narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Thabit said: A man's brother's death was announced to Salt ibn Ushaym, but he found him eating. He said: "Come near and eat, for my brother's death was announced to me some time ago."

He said: "How? I was the first to bring you the news." He said: "Allah the Exalted announced it to me, saying:" ﴿Indeed you are dying, and indeed they are dying﴾.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 15/254. The addition in the brackets is from it.]]

﴿Then indeed on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute with one another.﴾ That is, the righteous and the wrongdoer, the oppressor and the oppressed.

al-Zubayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will what was between us in this world be repeated to us, along with the particular sins?"

He said: "Yes, it will certainly be repeated upon you, until every person with a right is given his right."

Al-Zubayr said: "By Allah, the matter is indeed severe."[[Musnad Ahmad: 1/167; al-Mustadrak: 2/435.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 39, verses 40–52:**

﴿Upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment. Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind, with the truth. So whoever is guided, it is for his own self, and whoever goes astray, he strays only to its detriment. And you are not over them a guardian.﴾ "Guardian" here means one who watches over them and keeps account, and watches them and is vigilant over them. It was said: ﴿a guardian over them﴾, meaning one who compels them to belief.

﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾, that is, He seizes them at the end of their term and the completion of their allotted period. ﴿And those that have not died during their sleep﴾, as He takes the one who has died. He made sleep a kind of death. ﴿Then He withholds those on whom He has decreed death﴾, keeping them with Him.

The readers Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read ﴿quḍiya﴾ with a damma on the qaf, a kasra on the ḍad, and a fatha on the ya, with ﴿al-mawt﴾ in the nominative, following the passive form (Arabic: mā lam yusammi fā'iluhu, "the verb whose agent is not named").

The rest read it with a fatha on the qaf and ḍad. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading, and they said: because of His saying ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾, so it is He who decrees death upon them.

The exegetes said: the spirits of the living and the dead meet in sleep, and they get to know one another as much as Allah wills. When He wishes all of them to return to their bodies, Allah holds back the spirits of the dead with Him and confines them, and He releases the spirits of the living until they return to their bodies. [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 24/12.]]

﴿For a term appointed﴾, meaning the time when the period of their lives is completed. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Matari informed us: Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili informed us: Ibn Fudayl informed us: 'Ata' informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾. He said: He seizes the souls of the dead and the living; He withholds the souls of the dead and releases the souls of the living until a specified term, and He makes no error.

Ibn 'Abbas said: In the son of Adam there is a soul (nafs) and a spirit (rūḥ), between which is like the ray of the sun. The soul is that by which there is intellect and discernment, and the spirit is that by which there is life and movement. When the servant sleeps, Allah seizes his soul but does not seize his spirit.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Ma'dan informed us: Ibn Kasib informed us: Abdullah ibn Raja' informed us, from 'Ubaydullah, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When one of you goes to his bed, let him lie down on his right side and say: 'In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and in You I raise it. If You take my soul, then forgive it; and if You release it, then protect it with that with which You protect Your righteous servants.'" [134] [[Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah: 6/241; and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/262.]]

﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah?﴾ Say: ﴿Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?﴾ That is: even if they possess nothing of intercession and do not understand, you still worship them? ﴿Say: To Allah belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; then to Him you will be returned.﴾ ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Muqatil said: they were constricted.

Qatadah said: they disbelieved and were arrogant.

Al-Dahhak said: they recoiled.

Al-Kisa'i said: they were agitated.

Al-Mu'arrikh said: they denied. The root of al-ishmi'zaz is aversion and turning away.

'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

"When the sword-cutter bites with it, they shrink, and it turns them back, a hard and forceful one."  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/264; Lisan al-'Arab: 13/286.]]

﴿And when those besides Him are mentioned﴾, that is, the idols. This happened when Satan cast into the recitation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), during his recitation of Surah al-Najm, the words: "Those are the exalted cranes, whose intercession is hoped for." ﴿Then they rejoice﴾, meaning they become happy. ﴿Say: O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ.﴾ That is: O Originator of the heavens and the earth.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan informed us: 'Ubaydullah ibn Thabit informed us: Abu Sa'id al-Kindi informed us: Ibn Fudayl informed us: Salim ibn Abi Hafsah informed us, from Mundhir al-Thawri, who said:

I was with al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym when a man entered upon him who had been present at the killing of al-Husayn and had been among those who fought him. Ibn Khuthaym said: "O you who hung them" (meaning the heads). Then he put his hand into the man's mouth, under his tongue, and said: "By Allah, you killed a chosen group. **Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 39, verses 40–52:**

﴿Upon whom will come a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment. Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind, with the truth. So whoever is guided, it is for his own self, and whoever goes astray, he strays only to its detriment. And you are not over them a guardian.﴾ "Guardian" here means one who watches over them and keeps account, and watches them and is vigilant over them. It was said: ﴿a guardian over them﴾, meaning one who compels them to belief.

﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾, that is, He seizes them at the end of their term and the completion of their allotted period. ﴿And those that have not died during their sleep﴾, as He takes the one who has died. He made sleep a kind of death. ﴿Then He withholds those on whom He has decreed death﴾, keeping them with Him.

The readers Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read ﴿quḍiya﴾ with a damma on the qaf, a kasra on the ḍad, and a fatha on the ya, with ﴿al-mawt﴾ in the nominative, following the passive form (Arabic: mā lam yusammi fā'iluhu, "the verb whose agent is not named").

The rest read it with a fatha on the qaf and ḍad. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading, and they said: because of His saying ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾, so it is He who decrees death upon them.

The exegetes said: the spirits of the living and the dead meet in sleep, and they get to know one another as much as Allah wills. When He wishes all of them to return to their bodies, Allah holds back the spirits of the dead with Him and confines them, and He releases the spirits of the living until they return to their bodies. [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 24/12.]]

﴿For a term appointed﴾, meaning the time when the period of their lives is completed. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾

قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ the verse.

اختلف المفسرون في المعنيّين بهذه الآية.
The exegetes (tafsir scholars) differed concerning those intended by this verse.

فقال بعضهم: عنى بها قوما من المشركين.
Some of them said: it refers to a people among the polytheists.

قال ابن عبّاس: نزلت في أهل مكة قالوا يزعم محمّد انه من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ لم يغفر له، فكيف نهاجر ونسلم وقد عبدنا مع الله الها آخر وقتلنا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ؟ فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية.
Ibn ʿAbbas said: It was revealed concerning the people of Makkah, who said, "Muhammad claims that whoever worships idols and kills a soul which Allah has forbidden will not be forgiven. So how can we migrate and embrace Islam when we have worshipped another god besides Allah and killed the soul which Allah has forbidden?" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

أنبأني عبد الله بن حامد بن محمّد الأصفهاني أخبرني إبراهيم بن محمّد بن عبد الله البغدادي حدثنا أبو الحسن أحمد بن حمدان الجبلي حدثنا أبو إسماعيل حدثنا إسحاق بن سعيد أبو سلمة الدمشقي حدثنا أنس بن سفيان عن غالب بن عبد الله عن عطاء بن أبي رباح عن ابن عبّاس قال: بعث رسول الله ﷺ إلى وحشي يدعوه إلى الإسلام، فأرسل إليه: يا محمّد كيف تدعوني إلى دينك وأنت تزعم أنه من قتل أو شرك أو زنى يَلْقَ أَثاماً ويُضاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهاناً، وأنا قد فعلت ذلك كله، فهل تجد لي رخصة؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 60.]] الآية.
Abdullah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani informed me: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Baghdadi informed me: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Jabali narrated to us: Abu Ismail narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Saʿid Abu Salamah al-Dimashqi narrated to us: Anas ibn Sufyan narrated to us, from Ghalib ibn Abdullah, from ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent [a message] to Wahshi, inviting him to Islam. [Wahshi] sent back: "O Muhammad, how do you invite me to your religion when you claim that whoever kills, or associates partners with Allah, or commits fornication, will meet the penalty (athām), and the punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide in it humiliated? I have done all of that. Do you find any concession for me?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 60.]] the verse.

قال وحشي: هذا شرط شديد فلعلي لا أقدر على هذا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ [[Surah al-Nisaʾ: 48.]].
Wahshi said: "This is a severe condition; perhaps I will not be able to do this. Is there anything other than that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [[Surah al-Nisaʾ: 48.]].

فقال وحشي: هذا شرط شديد فلعلي لا أقدر على هذا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ﴾.
Wahshi said: "This is a severe condition; perhaps I will not be able to do this. Is there anything other than that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

فقال وحشي: أراني بعد في شبهة فلا أدري يغفر لي أم لا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾.
Wahshi said: "I still seem to be in doubt; I do not know whether He will forgive me or not. Is there anything other than that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾.

فقال وحشي: نعم هذه، فجاء فأسلم.
Wahshi said: "Yes, this one," so he came and embraced Islam.

فقال المسلمون: هذه له خاصة أم للمسلمين عامة؟
The Muslims said: "Is this specifically for him, or is it general for the Muslims?"

وقال: «بل للمسلمين عامة» [[al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 11/158; Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid: 10/215.]].
He said: "Rather, it is general for the Muslims."

وقال قتادة ذكر لنا أن ناسا أصابوا ذنوبا عظاما في الجاهلية، فلما جاء الإسلام أشفقوا أن لن يتاب عليهم، فدعاهم الله بهذه الآية.
Qatadah said: It has been mentioned to us that some people had committed grave sins in the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah). When Islam came, they feared that their repentance would not be accepted, so Allah called them with this verse.

وقال ابن عمر: نزلت هذه الآيات في عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر من المسلمين، كانوا أسلموا ثم فتنوا وعذبوا فافتتنوا فكنا نقول: لا يقبل الله تعالى من هؤلاء صرفا ولا عدلا أبدا، قوم أسلموا ثم تركوا دينهم بعذاب عذبوا به، فنزلت على هؤلاء الآيات فكان عمر بن الخطاب كاتبا فكتبها بيده، ثم بعث بها إلى عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد وإلى أولئك النفر فأسلموا وهاجروا.
Ibn ʿUmar said: These verses were revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and a group of Muslims who had embraced Islam, then were tested and tortured, and so they succumbed to the trial. We used to say: "Allah the Exalted will never accept from these people any repentance (ṣarf) or ransom (ʿadl), ever. They are a people who embraced Islam and then abandoned their religion because of the torment they were subjected to." Then these verses were revealed to them. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab was a scribe, so he wrote them with his own hand, then sent them to ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and those men. They embraced Islam and migrated.

أخبرنا أبو عبد الله بن فنجويه حدثنا أبو بكر بن خرجة حدثنا محمّد بن عبد الله بن سلمان الحضرمي حدثنا محمّد بن العلاء حدثنا يونس بن بكير حدثنا ابن إسحاق حدثنا نافع عن ابن عمر عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قال: لما اجتمعنا إلى الهجرة أبعدت أنا وعياش بن أبي ربيعة وهشام بن العاص بن وائل وقلنا: الميعاد بيننا المناصف ميقات بني غفار، فمن حبس منكم لم يأبها فقد حبس فليمض صاحبه، فأصبحت عندها أنا وعياش وحبس عنا هشام وفتن فافتتن، فقدمنا المدينة فكنا نقول: هل يقبل الله من هؤلاء توبة قوم عرفوا الله ورسوله ثم رجعوا عن ذلك لما أصابهم من الدّنيا؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوىً لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾.
