Abu ʿAbdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Kharjah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-ʿAlaʾ narrated to us: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Nafiʿ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: When we gathered for the migration, I, ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, and Hisham ibn al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il set out, and we said: "Our appointment between us is al-Manasif, the meeting-place of Banu Ghifar. Whoever of you is detained and does not come to it, has been detained; let his companion proceed." So I and ʿAyyash arrived there, but Hisham was detained and was tested, and he succumbed to the trial. We reached Madinah, and we used to say: "Will Allah accept the repentance of people who recognized Allah and His Messenger, then turned back from that because of what worldly affliction befell them?" Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the arrogant?﴾.

قال عمر: فكتبتها بيدي كتابا ثم بعثت بها إلى هشام.
ʿUmar said: I wrote it down with my own hand as a letter, then sent it to Hisham.

قال هشام: فلما قدمت عليّ خرجت بها إلى ذي طوى فقلت اللهم فهمنيها، فعرفت أنها أنزلت فينا، فرجعت فجلست على بعيري فلحقت برسول الله ﷺ.
Hisham said: When it reached me, I went out with it to Dhu Tuwa and said, "O Allah, make me understand it." I then understood that it had been revealed concerning us. So I returned, sat on my camel, and caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Hisham was later martyred at Ajnadayn during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.

وقال بعضهم: نزلت في قوم كانوا يرون أهل الكبائر من أهل النار، فأعلمهم الله تعالى أنه يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً لمن يشاء.
Some of them said: It was revealed concerning a people who used to regard the perpetrators of major sins as people of the Fire, so Allah the Exalted informed them that ﴿He forgives all sins for whomever He wills﴾.

وروى مقاتل بن حيان عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: كنا معشر أصحاب رسول الله نرى أو نقول: أنه ليس شيء من حسناتنا إلّا وهي مقبولة حتّى نزلت هذه الآية ﴿أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَلا تُبْطِلُوا أَعْمالَكُمْ﴾ فلما نزلت هذه الآية قلنا: ما هذا الذي يبطل أعمالنا؟ فقيل لنا:
Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: We, the companions of the Messenger of Allah, used to think, or say, that none of our good deeds would fail to be accepted, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds﴾. When this verse was revealed, we said: "What is this that nullifies our deeds?" It was said to us:
الكبائر والفواحش.
"The major sins and the gross immoralities."

قال: فكنا إذا رأينا من أصاب شيئا منها قلنا: قد هلك، فنزلت هذه الآية، فلما نزلت كففنا عن القول في ذلك، فكنا إذا رأينا أحدا أصاب منها شيئا خفنا عليه، وإن لم يصب منها شيئا رجونا له. وأراد بالإسراف ارتكاب الكبائر، والآية عامة للناس أجمعين لا تَقْنَطُوا.
He said: Whenever we saw someone commit any of them, we said, "He has perished." Then this verse was revealed, and after it was revealed we refrained from speaking about that. So whenever we saw someone who had committed any of them, we feared for him, and if he had not committed any of them, we hoped for him. The intended meaning of "transgression" (isrāf) here is the commission of major sins, and the verse is general for all people, in His words "do not despair".

قرأ أبو عمرو والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وعيسى والكسائي ويعقوب (لا تَقْنِطُوا) بكسر النون.
Abu ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, Yahya ibn Wathhab, ʿIsa, al-Kisaʾi, and Yaʿqub read (lā taqnaṭū) with a kasrah on the nūn.

وقرأ أشهب العقيلي: بضمه.
Ashhab al-ʿUqayli read it with a ḍammah on it.

وقرأ الآخرون: بفتحه.
The others read it with a fatḥah on it.

روى الأعمش عن أبي سعيد الأزدي عن أبي الكنود قال: دخل عبد الله بن مسعود المسجد فإذا قاص يقص وهو يذكر النار والأغلال، فجاء حتّى قام على رأسه وقال: يا مذكّر لم تقنط الناس ثم قرأ ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ الآية.
Al-Aʿmash narrated from Abu Saʿid al-Azdi, from Abu al-Kanud, who said: ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud entered the mosque and found a storyteller (qāṣṣ) narrating, mentioning the Fire and the shackles. He came and stood over him and said: "O reminder-giver, you are making people despair!" Then he recited: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ the verse.

أخبرنا ابن فنجويه حدثنا أبو حبش المقرئ حدثنا ابن فنجويه حدثنا عبد سلمة حدثنا عبد الرزاق أخبرنا معمر عن زيد بن أسلم: أن رجلا كان في الأمم الماضية يجتهد في العبادة فيشدد على نفسه ويقنّط الناس من رحمة الله ثم مات فقال: أي رب ما لي عندك؟
Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Habash the reciter narrated to us: Ibn Fanjawayh narrated to us: ʿAbd Salamah narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that a man in past nations used to strive hard in worship, making things hard on himself, and he made people despair of the mercy of Allah. Then he died, and said: "My Lord, what is my portion with You?"

قال: النار.
[Allah] said: "The Fire."

قال: أي رب وأين عبادتي واجتهادي؟
He said: "My Lord, where are my worship and my striving?"

فيقول: إنك كنت تقنط الناس من رحمتي في الدّنيا، فأنا اليوم أقنطك من رحمتي.
[Allah] says: "You used to make people despair of My mercy in the world, so today I make you despair of My mercy."

إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً.
﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾.

أخبرنا عبد الله بن حامد أخبرنا حامد بن محمّد بن عبد الله حدثنا محمّد بن صالح الأشج حدثنا داود بن إبراهيم حدثنا حماد بن سلمة حدثنا ثابت بن شهر بن حوشب عن أسماء بنت يزيد قالت: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: «قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً ولا يبالي» [135].
Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Hamid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed us: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Ashajj narrated to us: Dawud ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Thabit ibn Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, from Asma bint Yazid, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins,' and He does not mind."

وفي مصحف عبد الله: (إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء) .
In the codex of ʿAbdullah [ibn Masʿud]: "Indeed Allah forgives all sins for whomever He wills."

إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ.
﴿Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

أخبرنا ابن فنجويه حدثنا محمّد بن المظفر حدثنا عمرو بن علي حدثنا معاذ بن هشام حدثنا أبي عن عمرو بن مالك عن أبي الجوزاء قال: ما علمت أحدا من أهل العلم ولا من أصحاب محمّد ﷺ يقول لذنب: إن الله لا يغفر هذا.
Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Muzaffar narrated to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us: Muʿadh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza, who said: I do not know of anyone among the people of knowledge or among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ who said of any sin: "Allah will not forgive this."

أخبرنا عقيل بن محمّد بن أحمد: أن المعافا بن زكريا أخبرهم عن محمّد بن جرير حدثنا زكريا بن يحيى وهداد بن أبي زائدة حدثنا حجاج حدثنا ابن لهيعة عن أبي قنبل قال: سمعت أبا عبد الرحمن المزني يقول: حدثني أبو عبد الرحمن الجيلاني أنه سمع ثوبان مولى رسول الله ﷺ يقول: سمعت رسول الله (عليه السلام) : «يقول ما أحب أن لي الدّنيا وما فيها بهذه الآية قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ» [136].
Aqil ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us: that al-Muʿafa ibn Zakariyya informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Zakariyya ibn Yahya and Haddad ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us: Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, from Abu Qanbal, who said: I heard Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Muzani say: Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Jaylani told me that he heard Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: "I would not like to have this world and whatever is in it in exchange for this verse: ﴿Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful'﴾."

فقال رجل: يا رسول الله ومن أشرك؟
A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what about the one who associated partners [with Allah]?"

فسكت النبي (عليه السلام) ثم قال: «ألا ومن أشرك ألا ومن أشرك ألا ومن أشرك» [137] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/275.]].
The Prophet (peace be upon him) remained silent, then said: "Surely, and whoever associates partners! Surely, and whoever associates partners! Surely, and whoever associates partners!"

وبإسناده عن محمّد بن جرير حدثنا يعقوب حدثنا ابن علية حدثنا يونس عن ابن سيرين قال: قال علي رضي الله عنه: ما في القرآن آية أوسع من قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ الآية.
By his chain from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Yaʿqub narrated to us: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us: Yunus narrated to us, from Ibn Sirin, who said: ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an broader in scope than ﴿Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves'﴾ the verse."

وبه عن ابن جرير حدثنا ابن حميد حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن الشعبي عن شتير بن شكل قال: سمعت ابن مسعود يقول: إن أكثر آية فرجا في القرآن يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا الآية [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 24/20.]].
By the same chain from Ibn Jarir: Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Shaʿbi, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, who said: I heard Ibn Masʿud say: "The verse providing the most relief in the Qur'an is: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ the verse."

أخبرنا الحسين بن محمّد الحديثي حدثنا محمّد بن علي بن الحسن الصوفي حدثنا علي بن محمّد بن ماهان حدثنا سلمة بن شبيب قال: قريء على عبد الرزاق وأنا أسمع عن معمر عن الزهري قال: دخل عمر بن الخطاب على النبيّ ﷺ وهو يبكي فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: «ما يبكيك يا عمر؟» .
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi informed us: Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi narrated to us: ʿAli ibn Muhammad ibn Mahan narrated to us: Salamah ibn Shabib said: It was read out to ʿAbd al-Razzaq while I was listening, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was weeping, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What makes you weep, O ʿUmar?"

قال: يا رسول الله إن بالباب شابا قد أخرق فؤادي وهو يبكي.
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, at the door there is a young man who has torn my heart apart, and he is weeping."

فقال له رسول الله: «أدخله عليّ» .
The Messenger of Allah said to him: "Let him in to me."

فدخل وهو يبكي فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: «ما شأنك يا شاب؟» .
So he entered, weeping, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What is your matter, young man?"

قال: يا رسول الله أبكاني ذنوب كثيرة وخفت من جبار غضبان عليّ.
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, many sins have made me weep, and I fear a tyrant who is angry with me."

قال: «أشركت بالله يا شاب؟» .
He said: "Did you associate partners with Allah, young man?"

قال: لا.
He said: "No."

قال: «أقتلت نفسا بغير حقها؟» .
He said: "Did you kill a soul without right?"

قال: لا.
He said: "No."

قال: «فإن الله يغفر لك ذنبك ولو مثل السماوات السبع والأرضين السبع والجبال الرواسي» .
He said: "Then Allah will forgive your sin, even if it were like the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the firm mountains."

قال: يا رسول الله ذنب من ذنوبي أعظم من السماوات السبع ومن الأرضين السبع.
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, one of my sins is greater than the seven heavens and the seven earths."

قال: «ذنبك أعظم أم العرش؟» قال: ذنبي.
He said: "Is your sin greater, or the Throne?" He said: "My sin."

قال: «ذنبك أعظم أم الكرسي؟» .
He said: "Is your sin greater, or the Footstool (Kursi)?"

قال: ذنبي.
He said: "My sin."

قال: «ذنبك أعظم أم إلهك؟» .
He said: "Is your sin greater, or your God?"

قال: بل الله أجلّ وأعظم.
He said: "Rather, Allah is more majestic and greater."

فقال: «إن ربّنا لعظيم ولا يغفر الذنب العظيم إلّا الإله العظيم» .
Then he said: "Indeed our Lord is great, and none forgives a great sin except the Great God."

قال: «أخبرني عن ذنبك» .
He said: "Tell me about your sin."

قال: إني مستحيي من وجهك يا رسول الله.
He said: "I am ashamed before your face, O Messenger of Allah."

قال: «أخبرني ما ذنبك؟» .
He said: "Tell me, what is your sin?"

قال: إني كنت رجلا نباشا أنبش القبور منذ سبع سنين، حتّى ماتت جارية من بنات الأنصار فنبشت قبرها فأخرجتها من كفنها، ومضيت غير بعيد إذ غلبني الشيطان على نفسي، فرجعت فجامعتها ومضيت غير بعيد إذ قامت الجارية فقالت: الويل لك يا شاب من ديّان يوم الدين يوم يضع كرسيّه للقضاء، يأخذ للمظلوم من الظالم تركتني عريانة في عسكر الموتى ووقفتني جنبا بين يدي الله تعالى.
He said: "I was a grave-robber, digging up graves for seven years, until a young girl from the daughters of the Ansar died. I dug up her grave, took her out of her shroud, and walked off a short distance when Satan overpowered me. So I returned and had intercourse with her. Then I walked off a short distance when the girl stood up and said: 'Woe to you, young man, from the Judge of the Day of Judgment, the Day when He places His Footstool for judgment, taking from the oppressor for the oppressed. You left me naked in the army of the dead, and you stood me in a state of impurity before Allah the Exalted.'"

فقام رسول الله ﷺ وهو يضرب في قفاه ويقول: «يا فاسق أخرج ما أقربك من النار» .
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, striking the back of his neck and saying: "O sinner, get out! How close you are to the Fire!"

قال: فخرج الشاب تائبا إلى الله تعالى حتّى أتى عليه ما شاء الله ثم قال: يا إله محمّد وآدم وحواء إن كنت غفرت لي فاعلم محمدا وأصحابه وإلّا فأرسل نارا من السماء فأحرقني بها ونجني من عذاب الآخرة.
He said: The young man left, repentant to Allah the Exalted, until a period that Allah willed had passed over him. Then he said: "O God of Muhammad, Adam, and Eve, if You have forgiven me, then inform Muhammad and his companions; otherwise send a fire from the sky to burn me with it, and save me from the punishment of the Hereafter."

قال: فجاء جبرئيل وله جناحان جناح بالمشرق وجناح بالمغرب قال: السلام يقرؤك السلام. قال: «هو السلام وإليه يعود السلام» .
He said: Then Gabriel came, having two wings, one in the east and one in the west, and said: "Peace sends you greetings." [The Prophet] said: "He is Peace, and to Him returns peace."

قال: يقول: أنت خلقت خلقي؟.
[Gabriel] said: "He says: 'Did you create My creation?'"

قال: «لا، بل هو الذي خلقني» .
[The Prophet] said: "No, rather He is the One who created me."

قال: يقول: أنت ترزقهم؟
[Gabriel] said: "He says: 'Do you provide for them?'"

قال: «لا، بل هو يرزقني» .
[The Prophet] said: "No, rather He provides for me."

قال: أنت تتوب عليهم؟
[Gabriel] said: "Do you accept their repentance?"

قال: «لا، بل هو الذي يتوب عليّ» .
[The Prophet] said: "No, rather He is the One who accepts repentance from me."

قال: فتب على عبدي.
[Gabriel] said: "Then accept the repentance of Your servant."

قال: فدعا النبيّ ﷺ الشاب فتاب عليه وقال: «أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ» [[We have not found it among the sources available to us from the Sunni scholars; see: Amali al-Shaykh al-Saduq: 98.]].
He said: The Prophet ﷺ summoned the young man, accepted his repentance, and said: "Indeed Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful."

وَأَنِيبُوا إِلى رَبِّكُمْ أي واقبلوا وارجعوا إليه بالطاعة. وَأَسْلِمُوا لَهُ واخضعوا له مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ الْعَذابُ ثُمَّ لا تُنْصَرُونَ.
﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord﴾ means: accept and return to Him in obedience. ﴿And submit to Him﴾ means: humble yourselves before Him ﴿before the punishment comes upon you, and then you will not be helped﴾.

أخبرنا أبو عبد الله بن فنجويه الحافظ حدثنا أحمد بن محمّد بن إسحاق السنّي حدثنا أبو يعلى الموصلي حدثنا أبو خيثمة حدثنا أبو أحمد الزبيري حدثنا كثير بن زيد عن الحرث بن أبي يزيد قال: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله يقول: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «إن من السعادة أن يطول عمر العبد ويرزقه الله تعالى الإنابة» [138] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/332.]].
Abu ʿAbdullah ibn Fanjawayh al-Hafiz informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni narrated to us: Abu Yaʿla al-Mawsili narrated to us: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us: Kathir ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among happiness is that a servant's life is prolonged and Allah the Exalted grants him inābah (turning back to Him in repentance)."

وَاتَّبِعُوا أَحْسَنَ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ والقرآن كله حسن وانما معنى الآية ما قال الحسن: التزموا طاعته واجتنبوا معصيته، فإن الذي أنزل على ثلاثة أوجه: ذكر القبيح لنجتنبه، وذكر الأدون لئلا نرغب فيه، وذكر الحسن لنؤثره.
﴿And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. The entire Qur'an is good, and the meaning of the verse is as al-Hasan said: "Adhere to His obedience and avoid His disobedience, for what has been revealed to us is in three forms: mention of the ugly so that we avoid it, mention of the lesser so that we do not desire it, and mention of the good so that we prefer it."

وكذلك قال السدي: الأحسن ما أمر الله به في الكتاب.
Likewise al-Suddi said: "The best is what Allah has commanded in the Book."

وقال ابن زيد (وَاتَّبِعُوا أَحْسَنَ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) يعني المحكمات وكلوا علم المتشابهات إلى عالمها.
Ibn Zayd said: "﴿The best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ means the muhkamat (clear, unambiguous verses), and leave the knowledge of the mutashabihat (ambiguous verses) to the One who knows them."

مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ الْعَذابُ بَغْتَةً وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ أَنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يعني لأن لا تقول كقوله: أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ [[Surah al-Nahl: 15.]] وَأَنْ تَصُومُوا [[Surah al-Baqarah: 184.]] ونحوهما.
﴿Before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive, lest a soul say﴾ means: "lest a soul say," as in His saying ﴿lest it shake you﴾ [[Surah al-Nahl: 15.]] and ﴿that you fast﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 184.]] and similar examples.

يا حَسْرَتى يا ندامتا وحزني، والتحسر الاغتمام على ما فات، سمّي بذلك لانحساره عن صاحبه بما يمنع عليه استدراكه وتلا في الأمر فيه، والألف في قوله: (يا حَسْرَتى) هي بالكناية للمتكلم وإنما أريد يا حسرتي على الاضافة، ولكن العرب تحوّل الياء التي هي كناية اسم المتكلم في الاستغاثة ألفا فتقول: يا ويلتا ويا ندامتا، فيخرجون ذلك على لفظ الدعاء، وربّما لحقوا بها الهاء.
﴿Alas for my regret!﴾ means: "O my regret, O my remorse and my grief." Al-tahassur (regret) is distress over what has passed; it is so named because it leaves its owner dispossessed (inḥisār), with no way to make up for what has been lost. The alif in His words ﴿yā ḥasratā﴾ is the pronominal suffix of the speaker, though what is meant is "yā ḥasratī" with the possessive. But the Arabs convert the yāʾ, which is the pronoun of the first person, into an alif in invocation, saying "yā waylatā" and "yā nadāmatā," and so they render it in the form of a call. Sometimes they add a hāʾ to it.

أنشد الفراء:
Al-Farraʾ recited:

يا مرحباه بحمار ناجية ... إذا أتى قربته للسانية
"Welcome, O welcome to the riding-donkey of the she-camel, when it comes bringing its water-skin to the one who draws water."

وربّما الحقوا بها الياء بعد الألف ليدل على الإضافة.
Sometimes they also add a yāʾ after the alif to indicate the possessive.

وكذلك قرأ أبو جعفر: يا حسرتاي.
Likewise Abu Jaʿfar read: "yā ḥasratāy."

عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ قصّرت فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ قال الحسن: في طاعة الله. سعيد بن جبير:
﴿Over what I neglected﴾ means: "I fell short" ﴿in regard to Allah's side﴾. Al-Hasan said: "in obedience to Allah." Saʿid ibn Jubayr said:

في حق الله في أمر الله. قاله مجاهد.
"In the right of Allah, in the command of Allah." Mujahid said this.

قال أهل المعاني: هذا كما يقال هذا صغير في جنب ذلك الماضي، أي في أمره.
The scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: This is like saying, "This is small in comparison to that," meaning "in regard to that matter."

وقيل: في سبيل الله ودينه. والعرب تسمّي السبب والطريق الى الشيء جنبا تقول:
It was also said: "in the path of Allah and His religion." The Arabs call the means and path to something a "janb" (side), and they say:

تجرعت في جنبك غصصا وبلاء، أي بسببك ولأجلك.
"I swallowed in your janb bitter sorrows and afflictions," meaning: because of you and for your sake.

قال الشاعر:
The poet said:

أفي جنب بكر قطعتني ملامة ... لعمري لقد كانت ملامتها ثنى
"Because of [my affair with] Bakr, did blame cut me off? By my life, her blame was a fold (a passing matter)."

وقال في الجانب الذي يؤدي إلى رضى الله تعالى وثوابه، والعرب تسمّي الجانب جنبا.
It was also said of the side that leads to Allah's pleasure and reward, for the Arabs call a side a janb.

قال الشاعر:
The poet said:

الناس جنب والأمير جنب
"The people are on one side, and the commander is on another side."

يعني الناس من جانب والأمير من جانب.
Meaning: the people on one side and the commander on another.

وَإِنْ كُنْتُ لَمِنَ السَّاخِرِينَ المستهزئين بدين الله تعالى وكتابه ورسوله والمؤمنين.
﴿And indeed I was among those who mocked﴾, meaning those who ridicule the religion of Allah the Exalted, His Book, His Messenger, and the believers.

قال قتادة: في هذه الآية لم يكفه ان ضيع طاعة الله تعالى، حتّى جعل يسخر بأهل طاعة الله.
Qatadah said concerning this verse: "It was not enough for him to neglect the obedience of Allah the Exalted, until he began to mock the people of obedience to Allah."

أخبرنا الحسين بن محمّد بن فنجويه حدثنا هارون بن محمّد حدثنا محمّد بن عبد العزيز حدثنا سلمة حدثنا أبو الورد الوزان عن إسماعيل عن أبي صالح: (يا حَسْرَتى عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ) قال: كان رجل عالم في بني إسرائيل ترك علمه وأخذ في الفسق، أتاه إبليس فقال له: لك عمر طويل فتمتع من الدّنيا ثم تب.
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us: Abu al-Ward al-Waззan narrated to us, from Ismaʿil, from Abu Salih, concerning ﴿Alas for my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah's side﴾, who said: There was a learned man among the Children of Israel who abandoned his knowledge and took to immorality. Iblis came to him and said: "You have a long life, so enjoy the world, then repent."

فأخذ في الفسق، وكان عنده مال فأنفق ماله في الفجور، فأتاه مالك الموت في ألذّ ما كان.
So he persisted in immorality, and he had wealth, which he spent on debauchery. Then the Angel of Death came to him while he was at his most pleasurable state.

فقال: من أنت؟
He said: "Who are you?"

فقال: أنا ملك الموت جئت لأقبض روحك.
[The angel] said: "I am the Angel of Death; I have come to seize your soul."

فقال: يا حَسْرَتى عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ، ذهب عمري في طاعة الشيطان وأسخطت ربّي.
He said: "﴿Alas for my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah's side﴾! My life has passed in obedience to Satan, and I have angered my Lord."

فندم حين لم تنفعه الندامة، قال: فأنزل الله سبحانه وتعالى خبره في القرآن.
He repented when repentance no longer benefited him. He said: So Allah, glorified and exalted, revealed his account in the Qur'an.

أَوْ تَقُولَ لَوْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي لَكُنْتُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ أَوْ تَقُولَ حِينَ تَرَى الْعَذابَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِي كَرَّةً رجعة إلى الدّنيا فَأَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ وفي نصب قوله: (فَأَكُونَ) وجهان: أحدهما: على جواب لو.
﴿Or lest it say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous." Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had a return (karrah), a return to the world, so that I might be among the good-doers."﴾ Regarding the accusative in His words ﴿fa-akūna﴾, there are two possibilities. The first: it is an answer to "law" (if only).

والثاني: على الرد على موضع الكرّة، وتوجيه الكرّة في المعنى لو أنّ لي أن أكر.
The second: it is a reply to the position of "karrah" (return), and the meaning of "karrah" is "if only I could return."

كقول الشاعر: أنشده الفراء:
Like the poet's saying, which al-Farraʾ recited:

فمالك منها غير ذكرى وحسرة ... وتسأل عن ركبانها أين يمموا
"You have nothing from her except remembrance and regret, and you ask about her riders, where they headed."

فنصب تسأل عطفا على موضع الذكرى، لأن معنى الكلام: فمالك منها إلّا أن يذكر، ومنه قول الله تعالى: أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا [[Surah al-Shura: 51.]] عطف يرسل على موضع الوحي في قوله تعالى: إِلَّا وَحْياً.
Here "tasʾalu" is in the accusative by coordination with the position of "dhikrā" (remembrance), since the meaning of the statement is: "You have nothing from her except remembrance." From this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿or He sends a messenger﴾ [[Surah al-Shura: 51.]], where "yursila" is coordinated with the position of "waḥy" (revelation) in His saying ﴿except by revelation﴾.

بَلى قَدْ جاءَتْكَ آياتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِها وَاسْتَكْبَرْتَ وَكُنْتَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ.
﴿Yes! My signs had certainly come to you, but you denied them, and you were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 39, verses 53–64 (part 2 of 2):**

The common readers (al-ʿāmma) read ﴿يَا حَسْرَتَا﴾ and similar forms with the kāf and tā' vowelled with fatḥa. ʿĀʾisha read them with kasra throughout, bringing them back to the self (al-nafs). This is also reported from the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Ibn Fanjawayh narrated to us: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us: Saʿīd ibn Nuṣayr narrated to us, saying: I heard Isḥāq ibn Salama al-Rāzī say: I heard Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī mention, on the authority of al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed me: Saʿīda bint Ḥafṣ ibn al-Muhtadī informed us in Bukhara, saying: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad al-Baghdādī narrated to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus ibn Bukayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Māhān, Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī, narrated to us, on the authority of al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, on the authority of Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) say: "Yes! My signs did come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers." [139] [[Maʿānī al-Qurʾān: 6/187; al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/333.]] This is in address to the self.

Al-Marwazī said: This is also the transmission of al-Suraysī from al-Kisā'ī.

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, who claimed that He has a son and a partner, their faces blackened.﴾

Al-Akhfash said: "Tarā" (you see) does not govern "wujūhuhum muswaddatun" (their faces are blackened). Rather, it is an inceptive subject and predicate (mubtadaʾ and khabar).

﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾ ﴿And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him with their salvation (bi-mafāzatihim).﴾

The people of Kufa read "bi-mafāzātihim" with an alif, as a plural. The rest read it without an alif, as a singular. Abū ʿUbayd, Abū Ḥātim and al-Akhfash preferred this reading, because mafāza here means "the success" (al-fawz), and the meaning of the verse is: by their deliverance from punishment through their good deeds.

﴿No harm will touch them﴾, i.e., no hardship will reach them, ﴿nor will they grieve.﴾

﴿God is the Creator of all things, and He is over all things a Guardian.﴾ ﴿To Him belong the keys (maqālīd) of the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is, the keys to the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. Its singular is miqlād, like miftāḥ (key) with the plural mafātīḥ, and miqlīd with the plural manādīl. There is another form, aqālīd, whose singular is iqlīd. It was also said that it is a Persian word, arabicized from "iklīl" (crown).

Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Fanjawayh al-Dīnawarī informed us, with my reading to him: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Shanba narrated to us: Abū Ḥāmid Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar al-Mustamlī narrated to us: ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad ibn Shanba narrated to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated to us: Aghlab ibn Tamīm narrated to us, on the authority of Mukhallad Abū al-Hudhayl, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān his brother. Ibn ʿUyayna said: on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, on the authority of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may God be pleased with him), that he asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the interpretation of this verse: "To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth."

He said: "O ʿUthmān, no one has asked me about it before you. Its interpretation: there is no god but God, God is greatest, glory be to God and praise be to Him, and I seek God's forgiveness. There is no power except with God. He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. In His hand is the good. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things capable. O ʿUthmān, whoever says these when he reaches the morning or the evening, ten times, God grants him six qualities. As for the first: he is guarded from Iblīs and his troops. The second: twelve angels attend him. The third: he is given two qintārs (large measures) in Paradise. The fourth: a degree is raised for him. The fifth: God marries him to a wife among the wide-eyed maidens (al-ḥūr al-ʿīn). The sixth: he receives a reward like one who has recited the Qurʾān, the Torah and the Gospel, and he also receives a reward like one who has performed the ḥajj or ʿumra, and his pilgrimage and ʿumra are accepted. If he dies that night, he dies a martyr."[140] [[Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/115.]]

Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAdl informed us, with my reading to him: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us: Abū al-Ḥasan Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zakariyyā al-Jurjānī the jurist narrated to us: Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Naṣr al-Rāzī narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Nawfalī narrated to us: Ḥammād ibn Muḥammad al-Marwazī narrated to us: Abū ʿIṣma Nūḥ ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, on the authority of Abū Isḥāq, on the authority of al-Ḥārith, on the authority of ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him), who said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the interpretation of "al-maqālīd."

He said: "O ʿAlī, you have asked about something great. The maqālīd is that you say ten times when you reach the morning and ten times when you reach the evening:

There is no god but God, God is greatest, glory be to God, praise be to God, I seek God's forgiveness, and there is no power or might except with God... He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise... He gives life and causes death. In His hand is the good, and He is over all things capable. Whoever says them ten times when he reaches the morning and ten times when he reaches the evening, God grants him six qualities. The first of them: He guards him from Iblīs and his troops, so they have no authority over him. The second: he is given a qintār in Paradise, heavier in his scale than Mount Uhud. The third: God raises him a degree that none attains except the righteous. The fourth: God marries him to wide-eyed maidens. The fifth: twelve thousand angels witness for him, writing it in a scroll unrolled (fī raqqin manshūr), bearing witness for him on the Day of Resurrection. The sixth: it is as if he had recited the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the Furqān, and it is as if he had performed the ḥajj and ʿumra, and God accepts his pilgrimage and ʿumra. If he dies that day, or that night, or that month, he is sealed with the seal of the martyrs. This is the interpretation of the maqālīd."[141] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 15/275.]]

﴿Those who disbelieve in the signs of God, those are the losers.﴾ ﴿Say: Do you order me to worship other than God, O ignorant ones?﴾ This was when he called them to the religion of their fathers.

The readers differed over His saying "tamurūnnī" (you order me). The people of Medina read it with a single nūn, lightened, by elision (al-ḥadhf) and full articulation (al-taḥqīq).

The people of Syria read it with two nūns, in the original form (al-aṣl).

The rest read it with a single nūn, doubled, by assimilation (al-idghām).

قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ the verse.

اختلف المفسرون في المعنيّين بهذه الآية.
The exegetes (tafsir scholars) differed concerning those intended by this verse.

فقال بعضهم: عنى بها قوما من المشركين.
Some of them said: it refers to a people among the polytheists.

قال ابن عبّاس: نزلت في أهل مكة قالوا يزعم محمّد انه من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ لم يغفر له، فكيف نهاجر ونسلم وقد عبدنا مع الله الها آخر وقتلنا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ؟ فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية.
Ibn ʿAbbas said: It was revealed concerning the people of Makkah, who said, "Muhammad claims that whoever worships idols and kills a soul which Allah has forbidden will not be forgiven. So how can we migrate and embrace Islam when we have worshipped another god besides Allah and killed the soul which Allah has forbidden?" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

أنبأني عبد الله بن حامد بن محمّد الأصفهاني أخبرني إبراهيم بن محمّد بن عبد الله البغدادي حدثنا أبو الحسن أحمد بن حمدان الجبلي حدثنا أبو إسماعيل حدثنا إسحاق بن سعيد أبو سلمة الدمشقي حدثنا أنس بن سفيان عن غالب بن عبد الله عن عطاء بن أبي رباح عن ابن عبّاس قال: بعث رسول الله ﷺ إلى وحشي يدعوه إلى الإسلام، فأرسل إليه: يا محمّد كيف تدعوني إلى دينك وأنت تزعم أنه من قتل أو شرك أو زنى يَلْقَ أَثاماً ويُضاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهاناً، وأنا قد فعلت ذلك كله، فهل تجد لي رخصة؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 60.]] الآية.
Abdullah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani informed me: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Baghdadi informed me: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Jabali narrated to us: Abu Ismail narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Saʿid Abu Salamah al-Dimashqi narrated to us: Anas ibn Sufyan narrated to us, from Ghalib ibn Abdullah, from ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent [a message] to Wahshi, inviting him to Islam. [Wahshi] sent back: "O Muhammad, how do you invite me to your religion when you claim that whoever kills, or associates partners with Allah, or commits fornication, will meet the penalty (athām), and the punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide in it humiliated? I have done all of that. Do you find any concession for me?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 60.]] the verse.

قال وحشي: هذا شرط شديد فلعلي لا أقدر على هذا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ [[Surah al-Nisaʾ: 48.]].
Wahshi said: "This is a severe condition; perhaps I will not be able to do this. Is there anything other than that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [[Surah al-Nisaʾ: 48.]].

فقال وحشي: هذا شرط شديد فلعلي لا أقدر على هذا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ﴾.
Wahshi said: "This is a severe condition; perhaps I will not be able to do this. Is there anything other than that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

فقال وحشي: أراني بعد في شبهة فلا أدري يغفر لي أم لا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾.
Wahshi said: "I still seem to be in doubt; I do not know whether He will forgive me or not. Is there anything other than that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾.

فقال وحشي: نعم هذه، فجاء فأسلم.
Wahshi said: "Yes, this one," so he came and embraced Islam.

فقال المسلمون: هذه له خاصة أم للمسلمين عامة؟
The Muslims said: "Is this specifically for him, or is it general for the Muslims?"

وقال: «بل للمسلمين عامة» [[al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 11/158; Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid: 10/215.]].
He said: "Rather, it is general for the Muslims."

وقال قتادة ذكر لنا أن ناسا أصابوا ذنوبا عظاما في الجاهلية، فلما جاء الإسلام أشفقوا أن لن يتاب عليهم، فدعاهم الله بهذه الآية.
Qatadah said: It has been mentioned to us that some people had committed grave sins in the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah). When Islam came, they feared that their repentance would not be accepted, so Allah called them with this verse.

وقال ابن عمر: نزلت هذه الآيات في عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر من المسلمين، كانوا أسلموا ثم فتنوا وعذبوا فافتتنوا فكنا نقول: لا يقبل الله تعالى من هؤلاء صرفا ولا عدلا أبدا، قوم أسلموا ثم تركوا دينهم بعذاب عذبوا به، فنزلت على هؤلاء الآيات فكان عمر بن الخطاب كاتبا فكتبها بيده، ثم بعث بها إلى عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد وإلى أولئك النفر فأسلموا وهاجروا.
Ibn ʿUmar said: These verses were revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and a group of Muslims who had embraced Islam, then were tested and tortured, and so they succumbed to the trial. We used to say: "Allah the Exalted will never accept from these people any repentance (ṣarf) or ransom (ʿadl), ever. They are a people who embraced Islam and then abandoned their religion because of the torment they were subjected to." Then these verses were revealed to them. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab was a scribe, so he wrote them with his own hand, then sent them to ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and those men. They embraced Islam and migrated.

أخبرنا أبو عبد الله بن فنجويه حدثنا أبو بكر بن خرجة حدثنا محمّد بن عبد الله بن سلمان الحضرمي حدثنا محمّد بن العلاء حدثنا يونس بن بكير حدثنا ابن إسحاق حدثنا نافع عن ابن عمر عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قال: لما اجتمعنا إلى الهجرة أبعدت أنا وعياش بن أبي ربيعة وهشام بن العاص بن وائل وقلنا: الميعاد بيننا المناصف ميقات بني غفار، فمن حبس منكم لم يأبها فقد حبس فليمض صاحبه، فأصبحت عندها أنا وعياش وحبس عنا هشام وفتن فافتتن، فقدمنا المدينة فكنا نقول: هل يقبل الله من هؤلاء توبة قوم عرفوا الله ورسوله ثم رجعوا عن ذلك لما أصابهم من الدّنيا؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوىً لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾.
Abu ʿAbdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Kharjah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-ʿAlaʾ narrated to us: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Nafiʿ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: When we gathered for the migration, I, ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, and Hisham ibn al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il set out, and we said: "Our appointment between us is al-Manasif, the meeting-place of Banu Ghifar. Whoever of you is detained and does not come to it, has been detained; let his companion proceed." So I and ʿAyyash arrived there, but Hisham was detained and was tested, and he succumbed to the trial. We reached Madinah, and we used to say: "Will Allah accept the repentance of people who recognized Allah and His Messenger, then turned back from that because of what worldly affliction befell them?" Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the arrogant?﴾.

قال عمر: فكتبتها بيدي كتابا ثم بعثت بها إلى هشام.
ʿUmar said: I wrote it down with my own hand as a letter, then sent it to Hisham.

قال هشام: فلما قدمت عليّ خرجت بها إلى ذي طوى فقلت اللهم فهمنيها، فعرفت أنها أنزلت فينا، فرجعت فجلست على بعيري فلحقت برسول الله ﷺ.
Hisham said: When it reached me, I went out with it to Dhu Tuwa and said, "O Allah, make me understand it." I then understood that it had been revealed concerning us. So I returned, sat on my camel, and caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Hisham was later martyred at Ajnadayn during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.

وقال بعضهم: نزلت في قوم كانوا يرون أهل الكبائر من أهل النار، فأعلمهم الله تعالى أنه يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً لمن يشاء.
Some of them said: It was revealed concerning a people who used to regard the perpetrators of major sins as people of the Fire, so Allah the Exalted informed them that ﴿He forgives all sins for whomever He wills﴾.

وروى مقاتل بن حيان عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: كنا معشر أصحاب رسول الله نرى أو نقول: أنه ليس شيء من حسناتنا إلّا وهي مقبولة حتّى نزلت هذه الآية ﴿أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَلا تُبْطِلُوا أَعْمالَكُمْ﴾ فلما نزلت هذه الآية قلنا: ما هذا الذي يبطل أعمالنا؟ فقيل لنا:
Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: We, the companions of the Messenger of Allah, used to think, or say, that none of our good deeds would fail to be accepted, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds﴾. When this verse was revealed, we said: "What is this that nullifies our deeds?" It was said to us:
الكبائر والفواحش.
"The major sins and the gross immoralities."

قال: فكنا إذا رأينا من أصاب شيئا منها قلنا: قد هلك، فنزلت هذه الآية، فلما نزلت كففنا عن القول في ذلك، فكنا إذا رأينا أحدا أصاب منها شيئا خفنا عليه، وإن لم يصب منها شيئا رجونا له. وأراد بالإسراف ارتكاب الكبائر، والآية عامة للناس أجمعين لا تَقْنَطُوا.
He said: Whenever we saw someone commit any of them, we said, "He has perished." Then this verse was revealed, and after it was revealed we refrained from speaking about that. So whenever we saw someone who had committed any of them, we feared for him, and if he had not committed any of them, we hoped for him. The intended meaning of "transgression" (isrāf) here is the commission of major sins, and the verse is general for all people, in His words "do not despair".

قرأ أبو عمرو والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وعيسى والكسائي ويعقوب (لا تَقْنِطُوا) بكسر النون.
Abu ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, Yahya ibn Wathhab, ʿIsa, al-Kisaʾi, and Yaʿqub read (lā taqnaṭū) with a kasrah on the nūn.

وقرأ أشهب العقيلي: بضمه.
Ashhab al-ʿUqayli read it with a ḍammah on it.

وقرأ الآخرون: بفتحه.
The others read it with a fatḥah on it.

روى الأعمش عن أبي سعيد الأزدي عن أبي الكنود قال: دخل عبد الله بن مسعود المسجد فإذا قاص يقص وهو يذكر النار والأغلال، فجاء حتّى قام على رأسه وقال: يا مذكّر لم تقنط الناس ثم قرأ ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ الآية.
Al-Aʿmash narrated from Abu Saʿid al-Azdi, from Abu al-Kanud, who said: ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud entered the mosque and found a storyteller (qāṣṣ) narrating, mentioning the Fire and the shackles. He came and stood over him and said: "O reminder-giver, you are making people despair!" Then he recited: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ the verse.

أخبرنا ابن فنجويه حدثنا أبو حبش المقرئ حدثنا ابن فنجويه حدثنا عبد سلمة حدثنا عبد الرزاق أخبرنا معمر عن زيد بن أسلم: أن رجلا كان في الأمم الماضية يجتهد في العبادة فيشدد على نفسه ويقنّط الناس من رحمة الله ثم مات فقال: أي رب ما لي عندك؟
Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Habash the reciter narrated to us: Ibn Fanjawayh narrated to us: ʿAbd Salamah narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that a man in past nations used to strive hard in worship, making things hard on himself, and he made people despair of the mercy of Allah. Then he died, and said: "My Lord, what is my portion with You?"

قال: النار.
[Allah] said: "The Fire."

قال: أي رب وأين عبادتي واجتهادي؟
He said: "My Lord, where are my worship and my striving?"

فيقول: إنك كنت تقنط الناس من رحمتي في الدّنيا، فأنا اليوم أقنطك من رحمتي.
[Allah] says: "You used to make people despair of My mercy in the world, so today I make you despair of My mercy."

إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً.
﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾.

أخبرنا عبد الله بن حامد أخبرنا حامد بن محمّد بن عبد الله حدثنا محمّد بن صالح الأشج حدثنا داود بن إبراهيم حدثنا حماد بن سلمة حدثنا ثابت بن شهر بن حوشب عن أسماء بنت يزيد قالت: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: «قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً ولا يبالي» [135].
Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us: Hamid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed us: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Ashajj narrated to us: Dawud ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Thabit ibn Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, from Asma bint Yazid, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins,' and He does not mind."

وفي مصحف عبد الله: (إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء) .
In the codex of ʿAbdullah [ibn Masʿud]: "Indeed Allah forgives all sins for whomever He wills."

إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ.
﴿Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾.

أخبرنا ابن فنجويه حدثنا محمّد بن المظفر حدثنا عمرو بن علي حدثنا معاذ بن هشام حدثنا أبي عن عمرو بن مالك عن أبي الجوزاء قال: ما علمت أحدا من أهل العلم ولا من أصحاب محمّد ﷺ يقول لذنب: إن الله لا يغفر هذا.
Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Muzaffar narrated to us: ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us: Muʿadh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza, who said: I do not know of anyone among the people of knowledge or among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ who said of any sin: "Allah will not forgive this."

أخبرنا عقيل بن محمّد بن أحمد: أن المعافا بن زكريا أخبرهم عن محمّد بن جرير حدثنا زكريا بن يحيى وهداد بن أبي زائدة حدثنا حجاج حدثنا ابن لهيعة عن أبي قنبل قال: سمعت أبا عبد الرحمن المزني يقول: حدثني أبو عبد الرحمن الجيلاني أنه سمع ثوبان مولى رسول الله ﷺ يقول: سمعت رسول الله (عليه السلام) : «يقول ما أحب أن لي الدّنيا وما فيها بهذه الآية قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ» [136].
Aqil ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us: that al-Muʿafa ibn Zakariyya informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Zakariyya ibn Yahya and Haddad ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us: Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, from Abu Qanbal, who said: I heard Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Muzani say: Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Jaylani told me that he heard Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: "I would not like to have this world and whatever is in it in exchange for this verse: ﴿Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful'﴾."

فقال رجل: يا رسول الله ومن أشرك؟
A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what about the one who associated partners [with Allah]?"

فسكت النبي (عليه السلام) ثم قال: «ألا ومن أشرك ألا ومن أشرك ألا ومن أشرك» [137] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/275.]].
The Prophet (peace be upon him) remained silent, then said: "Surely, and whoever associates partners! Surely, and whoever associates partners! Surely, and whoever associates partners!"

وبإسناده عن محمّد بن جرير حدثنا يعقوب حدثنا ابن علية حدثنا يونس عن ابن سيرين قال: قال علي رضي الله عنه: ما في القرآن آية أوسع من قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ الآية.
By his chain from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Yaʿqub narrated to us: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us: Yunus narrated to us, from Ibn Sirin, who said: ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an broader in scope than ﴿Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves'﴾ the verse."

وبه عن ابن جرير حدثنا ابن حميد حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن الشعبي عن شتير بن شكل قال: سمعت ابن مسعود يقول: إن أكثر آية فرجا في القرآن يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا الآية [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 24/20.]].
By the same chain from Ibn Jarir: Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Shaʿbi, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, who said: I heard Ibn Masʿud say: "The verse providing the most relief in the Qur'an is: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ the verse."

أخبرنا الحسين بن محمّد الحديثي حدثنا محمّد بن علي بن الحسن الصوفي حدثنا علي بن محمّد بن ماهان حدثنا سلمة بن شبيب قال: قريء على عبد الرزاق وأنا أسمع عن معمر عن الزهري قال: دخل عمر بن الخطاب على النبيّ ﷺ وهو يبكي فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: «ما يبكيك يا عمر؟» .
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi informed us: Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi narrated to us: ʿAli ibn Muhammad ibn Mahan narrated to us: Salamah ibn Shabib said: It was read out to ʿAbd al-Razzaq while I was listening, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was weeping, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What makes you weep, O ʿUmar?"

قال: يا رسول الله إن بالباب شابا قد أخرق فؤادي وهو يبكي.
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, at the door there is a young man who has torn my heart apart, and he is weeping."

فقال له رسول الله: «أدخله عليّ» .
The Messenger of Allah said to him: "Let him in to me."

فدخل وهو يبكي فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: «ما شأنك يا شاب؟» .
So he entered, weeping, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What is your matter, young man?"

قال: يا رسول الله أبكاني ذنوب كثيرة وخفت من جبار غضبان عليّ.
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, many sins have made me weep, and I fear a tyrant who is angry with me."

قال: «أشركت بالله يا شاب؟» .
He said: "Did you associate partners with Allah, young man?"

قال: لا.
He said: "No."

قال: «أقتلت نفسا بغير حقها؟» .
He said: "Did you kill a soul without right?"

قال: لا.
He said: "No."

قال: «فإن الله يغفر لك ذنبك ولو مثل السماوات السبع والأرضين السبع والجبال الرواسي» .
He said: "Then Allah will forgive your sin, even if it were like the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the firm mountains."

قال: يا رسول الله ذنب من ذنوبي أعظم من السماوات السبع ومن الأرضين السبع.
He said: "O Messenger of Allah, one of my sins is greater than the seven heavens and the seven earths."

قال: «ذنبك أعظم أم العرش؟» قال: ذنبي.
He said: "Is your sin greater, or the Throne?" He said: "My sin."

قال: «ذنبك أعظم أم الكرسي؟» .
He said: "Is your sin greater, or the Footstool (Kursi)?"

قال: ذنبي.
He said: "My sin."

قال: «ذنبك أعظم أم إلهك؟» .
He said: "Is your sin greater, or your God?"

قال: بل الله أجلّ وأعظم.
He said: "Rather, Allah is more majestic and greater."

فقال: «إن ربّنا لعظيم ولا يغفر الذنب العظيم إلّا الإله العظيم» .
Then he said: "Indeed our Lord is great, and none forgives a great sin except the Great God."

قال: «أخبرني عن ذنبك» .
He said: "Tell me about your sin."

قال: إني مستحيي من وجهك يا رسول الله.
He said: "I am ashamed before your face, O Messenger of Allah."

قال: «أخبرني ما ذنبك؟» .
He said: "Tell me, what is your sin?"

قال: إني كنت رجلا نباشا أنبش القبور منذ سبع سنين، حتّى ماتت جارية من بنات الأنصار فنبشت قبرها فأخرجتها من كفنها، ومضيت غير بعيد إذ غلبني الشيطان على نفسي، فرجعت فجامعتها ومضيت غير بعيد إذ قامت الجارية فقالت: الويل لك يا شاب من ديّان يوم الدين يوم يضع كرسيّه للقضاء، يأخذ للمظلوم من الظالم تركتني عريانة في عسكر الموتى ووقفتني جنبا بين يدي الله تعالى.
He said: "I was a grave-robber, digging up graves for seven years, until a young girl from the daughters of the Ansar died. I dug up her grave, took her out of her shroud, and walked off a short distance when Satan overpowered me. So I returned and had intercourse with her. Then I walked off a short distance when the girl stood up and said: 'Woe to you, young man, from the Judge of the Day of Judgment, the Day when He places His Footstool for judgment, taking from the oppressor for the oppressed. You left me naked in the army of the dead, and you stood me in a state of impurity before Allah the Exalted.'"

فقام رسول الله ﷺ وهو يضرب في قفاه ويقول: «يا فاسق أخرج ما أقربك من النار» .
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, striking the back of his neck and saying: "O sinner, get out! How close you are to the Fire!"

قال: فخرج الشاب تائبا إلى الله تعالى حتّى أتى عليه ما شاء الله ثم قال: يا إله محمّد وآدم وحواء إن كنت غفرت لي فاعلم محمدا وأصحابه وإلّا فأرسل نارا من السماء فأحرقني بها ونجني من عذاب الآخرة.
He said: The young man left, repentant to Allah the Exalted, until a period that Allah willed had passed over him. Then he said: "O God of Muhammad, Adam, and Eve, if You have forgiven me, then inform Muhammad and his companions; otherwise send a fire from the sky to burn me with it, and save me from the punishment of the Hereafter."

قال: فجاء جبرئيل وله جناحان جناح بالمشرق وجناح بالمغرب قال: السلام يقرؤك السلام. قال: «هو السلام وإليه يعود السلام» .
He said: Then Gabriel came, having two wings, one in the east and one in the west, and said: "Peace sends you greetings." [The Prophet] said: "He is Peace, and to Him returns peace."

قال: يقول: أنت خلقت خلقي؟.
[Gabriel] said: "He says: 'Did you create My creation?'"

قال: «لا، بل هو الذي خلقني» .
[The Prophet] said: "No, rather He is the One who created me."

قال: يقول: أنت ترزقهم؟
[Gabriel] said: "He says: 'Do you provide for them?'"

قال: «لا، بل هو يرزقني» .
[The Prophet] said: "No, rather He provides for me."

قال: أنت تتوب عليهم؟
[Gabriel] said: "Do you accept their repentance?"

قال: «لا، بل هو الذي يتوب عليّ» .
[The Prophet] said: "No, rather He is the One who accepts repentance from me."

قال: فتب على عبدي.
[Gabriel] said: "Then accept the repentance of Your servant."

قال: فدعا النبيّ ﷺ الشاب فتاب عليه وقال: «أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ» [[We have not found it among the sources available to us from the Sunni scholars; see: Amali al-Shaykh al-Saduq: 98.]].
He said: The Prophet ﷺ summoned the young man, accepted his repentance, and said: "Indeed Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful."

وَأَنِيبُوا إِلى رَبِّكُمْ أي واقبلوا وارجعوا إليه بالطاعة. وَأَسْلِمُوا لَهُ واخضعوا له مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ الْعَذابُ ثُمَّ لا تُنْصَرُونَ.
﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord﴾ means: accept and return to Him in obedience. ﴿And submit to Him﴾ means: humble yourselves before Him ﴿before the punishment comes upon you, and then you will not be helped﴾.

أخبرنا أبو عبد الله بن فنجويه الحافظ حدثنا أحمد بن محمّد بن إسحاق السنّي حدثنا أبو يعلى الموصلي حدثنا أبو خيثمة حدثنا أبو أحمد الزبيري حدثنا كثير بن زيد عن الحرث بن أبي يزيد قال: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله يقول: قال رسول الله ﷺ: «إن من السعادة أن يطول عمر العبد ويرزقه الله تعالى الإنابة» [138] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/332.]].
Abu ʿAbdullah ibn Fanjawayh al-Hafiz informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni narrated to us: Abu Yaʿla al-Mawsili narrated to us: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us: Kathir ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among happiness is that a servant's life is prolonged and Allah the Exalted grants him inābah (turning back to Him in repentance)."

وَاتَّبِعُوا أَحْسَنَ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ والقرآن كله حسن وانما معنى الآية ما قال الحسن: التزموا طاعته واجتنبوا معصيته، فإن الذي أنزل على ثلاثة أوجه: ذكر القبيح لنجتنبه، وذكر الأدون لئلا نرغب فيه، وذكر الحسن لنؤثره.
﴿And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. The entire Qur'an is good, and the meaning of the verse is as al-Hasan said: "Adhere to His obedience and avoid His disobedience, for what has been revealed to us is in three forms: mention of the ugly so that we avoid it, mention of the lesser so that we do not desire it, and mention of the good so that we prefer it."

وكذلك قال السدي: الأحسن ما أمر الله به في الكتاب.
Likewise al-Suddi said: "The best is what Allah has commanded in the Book."

وقال ابن زيد (وَاتَّبِعُوا أَحْسَنَ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) يعني المحكمات وكلوا علم المتشابهات إلى عالمها.
Ibn Zayd said: "﴿The best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ means the muhkamat (clear, unambiguous verses), and leave the knowledge of the mutashabihat (ambiguous verses) to the One who knows them."

مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ الْعَذابُ بَغْتَةً وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ أَنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يعني لأن لا تقول كقوله: أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ [[Surah al-Nahl: 15.]] وَأَنْ تَصُومُوا [[Surah al-Baqarah: 184.]] ونحوهما.
﴿Before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive, lest a soul say﴾ means: "lest a soul say," as in His saying ﴿lest it shake you﴾ [[Surah al-Nahl: 15.]] and ﴿that you fast﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 184.]] and similar examples.

يا حَسْرَتى يا ندامتا وحزني، والتحسر الاغتمام على ما فات، سمّي بذلك لانحساره عن صاحبه بما يمنع عليه استدراكه وتلا في الأمر فيه، والألف في قوله: (يا حَسْرَتى) هي بالكناية للمتكلم وإنما أريد يا حسرتي على الاضافة، ولكن العرب تحوّل الياء التي هي كناية اسم المتكلم في الاستغاثة ألفا فتقول: يا ويلتا ويا ندامتا، فيخرجون ذلك على لفظ الدعاء، وربّما لحقوا بها الهاء.
﴿Alas for my regret!﴾ means: "O my regret, O my remorse and my grief." Al-tahassur (regret) is distress over what has passed; it is so named because it leaves its owner dispossessed (inḥisār), with no way to make up for what has been lost. The alif in His words ﴿yā ḥasratā﴾ is the pronominal suffix of the speaker, though what is meant is "yā ḥasratī" with the possessive. But the Arabs convert the yāʾ, which is the pronoun of the first person, into an alif in invocation, saying "yā waylatā" and "yā nadāmatā," and so they render it in the form of a call. Sometimes they add a hāʾ to it.

أنشد الفراء:
Al-Farraʾ recited:

يا مرحباه بحمار ناجية ... إذا أتى قربته للسانية
"Welcome, O welcome to the riding-donkey of the she-camel, when it comes bringing its water-skin to the one who draws water."

وربّما الحقوا بها الياء بعد الألف ليدل على الإضافة.
Sometimes they also add a yāʾ after the alif to indicate the possessive.

وكذلك قرأ أبو جعفر: يا حسرتاي.
Likewise Abu Jaʿfar read: "yā ḥasratāy."

عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ قصّرت فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ قال الحسن: في طاعة الله. سعيد بن جبير:
﴿Over what I neglected﴾ means: "I fell short" ﴿in regard to Allah's side﴾. Al-Hasan said: "in obedience to Allah." Saʿid ibn Jubayr said:

في حق الله في أمر الله. قاله مجاهد.
"In the right of Allah, in the command of Allah." Mujahid said this.

قال أهل المعاني: هذا كما يقال هذا صغير في جنب ذلك الماضي، أي في أمره.
The scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: This is like saying, "This is small in comparison to that," meaning "in regard to that matter."

وقيل: في سبيل الله ودينه. والعرب تسمّي السبب والطريق الى الشيء جنبا تقول:
It was also said: "in the path of Allah and His religion." The Arabs call the means and path to something a "janb" (side), and they say:

تجرعت في جنبك غصصا وبلاء، أي بسببك ولأجلك.
"I swallowed in your janb bitter sorrows and afflictions," meaning: because of you and for your sake.

قال الشاعر:
The poet said:

أفي جنب بكر قطعتني ملامة ... لعمري لقد كانت ملامتها ثنى
"Because of [my affair with] Bakr, did blame cut me off? By my life, her blame was a fold (a passing matter)."

وقال في الجانب الذي يؤدي إلى رضى الله تعالى وثوابه، والعرب تسمّي الجانب جنبا.
It was also said of the side that leads to Allah's pleasure and reward, for the Arabs call a side a janb.

قال الشاعر:
The poet said:

الناس جنب والأمير جنب
"The people are on one side, and the commander is on another side."

يعني الناس من جانب والأمير من جانب.
Meaning: the people on one side and the commander on another.

وَإِنْ كُنْتُ لَمِنَ السَّاخِرِينَ المستهزئين بدين الله تعالى وكتابه ورسوله والمؤمنين.
﴿And indeed I was among those who mocked﴾, meaning those who ridicule the religion of Allah the Exalted, His Book, His Messenger, and the believers.

قال قتادة: في هذه الآية لم يكفه ان ضيع طاعة الله تعالى، حتّى جعل يسخر بأهل طاعة الله.
Qatadah said concerning this verse: "It was not enough for him to neglect the obedience of Allah the Exalted, until he began to mock the people of obedience to Allah."

أخبرنا الحسين بن محمّد بن فنجويه حدثنا هارون بن محمّد حدثنا محمّد بن عبد العزيز حدثنا سلمة حدثنا أبو الورد الوزان عن إسماعيل عن أبي صالح: (يا حَسْرَتى عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ) قال: كان رجل عالم في بني إسرائيل ترك علمه وأخذ في الفسق، أتاه إبليس فقال له: لك عمر طويل فتمتع من الدّنيا ثم تب.
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us: Abu al-Ward al-Waззan narrated to us, from Ismaʿil, from Abu Salih, concerning ﴿Alas for my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah's side﴾, who said: There was a learned man among the Children of Israel who abandoned his knowledge and took to immorality. Iblis came to him and said: "You have a long life, so enjoy the world, then repent."

فأخذ في الفسق، وكان عنده مال فأنفق ماله في الفجور، فأتاه مالك الموت في ألذّ ما كان.
So he persisted in immorality, and he had wealth, which he spent on debauchery. Then the Angel of Death came to him while he was at his most pleasurable state.

فقال: من أنت؟
He said: "Who are you?"

فقال: أنا ملك الموت جئت لأقبض روحك.
[The angel] said: "I am the Angel of Death; I have come to seize your soul."

فقال: يا حَسْرَتى عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ، ذهب عمري في طاعة الشيطان وأسخطت ربّي.
He said: "﴿Alas for my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah's side﴾! My life has passed in obedience to Satan, and I have angered my Lord."

فندم حين لم تنفعه الندامة، قال: فأنزل الله سبحانه وتعالى خبره في القرآن.
He repented when repentance no longer benefited him. He said: So Allah, glorified and exalted, revealed his account in the Qur'an.

أَوْ تَقُولَ لَوْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي لَكُنْتُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ أَوْ تَقُولَ حِينَ تَرَى الْعَذابَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِي كَرَّةً رجعة إلى الدّنيا فَأَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ وفي نصب قوله: (فَأَكُونَ) وجهان: أحدهما: على جواب لو.
﴿Or lest it say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous." Or lest it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had a return (karrah), a return to the world, so that I might be among the good-doers."﴾ Regarding the accusative in His words ﴿fa-akūna﴾, there are two possibilities. The first: it is an answer to "law" (if only).

والثاني: على الرد على موضع الكرّة، وتوجيه الكرّة في المعنى لو أنّ لي أن أكر.
The second: it is a reply to the position of "karrah" (return), and the meaning of "karrah" is "if only I could return."

كقول الشاعر: أنشده الفراء:
Like the poet's saying, which al-Farraʾ recited:

فمالك منها غير ذكرى وحسرة ... وتسأل عن ركبانها أين يمموا
"You have nothing from her except remembrance and regret, and you ask about her riders, where they headed."

فنصب تسأل عطفا على موضع الذكرى، لأن معنى الكلام: فمالك منها إلّا أن يذكر، ومنه قول الله تعالى: أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا [[Surah al-Shura: 51.]] عطف يرسل على موضع الوحي في قوله تعالى: إِلَّا وَحْياً.
Here "tasʾalu" is in the accusative by coordination with the position of "dhikrā" (remembrance), since the meaning of the statement is: "You have nothing from her except remembrance." From this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿or He sends a messenger﴾ [[Surah al-Shura: 51.]], where "yursila" is coordinated with the position of "waḥy" (revelation) in His saying ﴿except by revelation﴾.

بَلى قَدْ جاءَتْكَ آياتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِها وَاسْتَكْبَرْتَ وَكُنْتَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ.
﴿Yes! My signs had certainly come to you, but you denied them, and you were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 39, verses 53–64 (part 2 of 2):**

The common readers (al-ʿāmma) read ﴿يَا حَسْرَتَا﴾ and similar forms with the kāf and tā' vowelled with fatḥa. ʿĀʾisha read them with kasra throughout, bringing them back to the self (al-nafs). This is also reported from the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Ibn Fanjawayh narrated to us: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us: Saʿīd ibn Nuṣayr narrated to us, saying: I heard Isḥāq ibn Salama al-Rāzī say: I heard Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī mention, on the authority of al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed me: Saʿīda bint Ḥafṣ ibn al-Muhtadī informed us in Bukhara, saying: Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad al-Baghdādī narrated to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus ibn Bukayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Māhān, Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī, narrated to us, on the authority of al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, on the authority of Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) say: "Yes! My signs did come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers." [139] [[Maʿānī al-Qurʾān: 6/187; al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/333.]] This is in address to the self.

Al-Marwazī said: This is also the transmission of al-Suraysī from al-Kisā'ī.

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, who claimed that He has a son and a partner, their faces blackened.﴾

Al-Akhfash said: "Tarā" (you see) does not govern "wujūhuhum muswaddatun" (their faces are blackened). Rather, it is an inceptive subject and predicate (mubtadaʾ and khabar).

﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾ ﴿And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him with their salvation (bi-mafāzatihim).﴾

The people of Kufa read "bi-mafāzātihim" with an alif, as a plural. The rest read it without an alif, as a singular. Abū ʿUbayd, Abū Ḥātim and al-Akhfash preferred this reading, because mafāza here means "the success" (al-fawz), and the meaning of the verse is: by their deliverance from punishment through their good deeds.

﴿No harm will touch them﴾, i.e., no hardship will reach them, ﴿nor will they grieve.﴾

﴿God is the Creator of all things, and He is over all things a Guardian.﴾ ﴿To Him belong the keys (maqālīd) of the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is, the keys to the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. Its singular is miqlād, like miftāḥ (key) with the plural mafātīḥ, and miqlīd with the plural manādīl. There is another form, aqālīd, whose singular is iqlīd. It was also said that it is a Persian word, arabicized from "iklīl" (crown).

Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Fanjawayh al-Dīnawarī informed us, with my reading to him: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Shanba narrated to us: Abū Ḥāmid Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar al-Mustamlī narrated to us: ʿUmar ibn Aḥmad ibn Shanba narrated to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated to us: Aghlab ibn Tamīm narrated to us, on the authority of Mukhallad Abū al-Hudhayl, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān his brother. Ibn ʿUyayna said: on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, on the authority of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may God be pleased with him), that he asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the interpretation of this verse: "To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth."

He said: "O ʿUthmān, no one has asked me about it before you. Its interpretation: there is no god but God, God is greatest, glory be to God and praise be to Him, and I seek God's forgiveness. There is no power except with God. He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. In His hand is the good. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things capable. O ʿUthmān, whoever says these when he reaches the morning or the evening, ten times, God grants him six qualities. As for the first: he is guarded from Iblīs and his troops. The second: twelve angels attend him. The third: he is given two qintārs (large measures) in Paradise. The fourth: a degree is raised for him. The fifth: God marries him to a wife among the wide-eyed maidens (al-ḥūr al-ʿīn). The sixth: he receives a reward like one who has recited the Qurʾān, the Torah and the Gospel, and he also receives a reward like one who has performed the ḥajj or ʿumra, and his pilgrimage and ʿumra are accepted. If he dies that night, he dies a martyr."[140] [[Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 10/115.]]

Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAdl informed us, with my reading to him: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us: Abū al-Ḥasan Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zakariyyā al-Jurjānī the jurist narrated to us: Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Naṣr al-Rāzī narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Nawfalī narrated to us: Ḥammād ibn Muḥammad al-Marwazī narrated to us: Abū ʿIṣma Nūḥ ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, on the authority of Abū Isḥāq, on the authority of al-Ḥārith, on the authority of ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him), who said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the interpretation of "al-maqālīd."

He said: "O ʿAlī, you have asked about something great. The maqālīd is that you say ten times when you reach the morning and ten times when you reach the evening:

There is no god but God, God is greatest, glory be to God, praise be to God, I seek God's forgiveness, and there is no power or might except with God... He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise... He gives life and causes death. In His hand is the good, and He is over all things capable. Whoever says them ten times when he reaches the morning and ten times when he reaches the evening, God grants him six qualities. The first of them: He guards him from Iblīs and his troops, so they have no authority over him. The second: he is given a qintār in Paradise, heavier in his scale than Mount Uhud. The third: God raises him a degree that none attains except the righteous. The fourth: God marries him to wide-eyed maidens. The fifth: twelve thousand angels witness for him, writing it in a scroll unrolled (fī raqqin manshūr), bearing witness for him on the Day of Resurrection. The sixth: it is as if he had recited the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the Furqān, and it is as if he had performed the ḥajj and ʿumra, and God accepts his pilgrimage and ʿumra. If he dies that day, or that night, or that month, he is sealed with the seal of the martyrs. This is the interpretation of the maqālīd."[141] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 15/275.]]

﴿Those who disbelieve in the signs of God, those are the losers.﴾ ﴿Say: Do you order me to worship other than God, O ignorant ones?﴾ This was when he called them to the religion of their fathers.

The readers differed over His saying "tamurūnnī" (you order me). The people of Medina read it with a single nūn, lightened, by elision (al-ḥadhf) and full articulation (al-taḥqīq).

The people of Syria read it with two nūns, in the original form (al-aṣl).

The rest read it with a single nūn, doubled, by assimilation (al-idghām).

قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ the verse.

اختلف المفسرون في المعنيّين بهذه الآية.
The exegetes (tafsir scholars) differed concerning those intended by this verse.

فقال بعضهم: عنى بها قوما من المشركين.
Some of them said: it refers to a people among the polytheists.

قال ابن عبّاس: نزلت في أهل مكة قالوا يزعم محمّد انه من عبد الأوثان وقتل النفس الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ لم يغفر له، فكيف نهاجر ونسلم وقد عبدنا مع الله الها آخر وقتلنا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ؟ فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية.
Ibn ʿAbbas said: It was revealed concerning the people of Makkah, who said, "Muhammad claims that whoever worships idols and kills a soul which Allah has forbidden will not be forgiven. So how can we migrate and embrace Islam when we have worshipped another god besides Allah and killed the soul which Allah has forbidden?" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

أنبأني عبد الله بن حامد بن محمّد الأصفهاني أخبرني إبراهيم بن محمّد بن عبد الله البغدادي حدثنا أبو الحسن أحمد بن حمدان الجبلي حدثنا أبو إسماعيل حدثنا إسحاق بن سعيد أبو سلمة الدمشقي حدثنا أنس بن سفيان عن غالب بن عبد الله عن عطاء بن أبي رباح عن ابن عبّاس قال: بعث رسول الله ﷺ إلى وحشي يدعوه إلى الإسلام، فأرسل إليه: يا محمّد كيف تدعوني إلى دينك وأنت تزعم أنه من قتل أو شرك أو زنى يَلْقَ أَثاماً ويُضاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهاناً، وأنا قد فعلت ذلك كله، فهل تجد لي رخصة؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 60.]] الآية.
Abdullah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani informed me: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Baghdadi informed me: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Jabali narrated to us: Abu Ismail narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Saʿid Abu Salamah al-Dimashqi narrated to us: Anas ibn Sufyan narrated to us, from Ghalib ibn Abdullah, from ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent [a message] to Wahshi, inviting him to Islam. [Wahshi] sent back: "O Muhammad, how do you invite me to your religion when you claim that whoever kills, or associates partners with Allah, or commits fornication, will meet the penalty (athām), and the punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide in it humiliated? I have done all of that. Do you find any concession for me?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 60.]] the verse.

قال وحشي: هذا شرط شديد فلعلي لا أقدر على هذا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ [[Surah al-Nisaʾ: 48.]].
Wahshi said: "This is a severe condition; perhaps I will not be able to do this. Is there anything other than that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [[Surah al-Nisaʾ: 48.]].

فقال وحشي: هذا شرط شديد فلعلي لا أقدر على هذا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ﴾.
Wahshi said: "This is a severe condition; perhaps I will not be able to do this. Is there anything other than that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

فقال وحشي: أراني بعد في شبهة فلا أدري يغفر لي أم لا، فهل غير ذلك؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾.
Wahshi said: "I still seem to be in doubt; I do not know whether He will forgive me or not. Is there anything other than that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾.

فقال وحشي: نعم هذه، فجاء فأسلم.
Wahshi said: "Yes, this one," so he came and embraced Islam.

فقال المسلمون: هذه له خاصة أم للمسلمين عامة؟
The Muslims said: "Is this specifically for him, or is it general for the Muslims?"

وقال: «بل للمسلمين عامة» [[al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 11/158; Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid: 10/215.]].
He said: "Rather, it is general for the Muslims."

وقال قتادة ذكر لنا أن ناسا أصابوا ذنوبا عظاما في الجاهلية، فلما جاء الإسلام أشفقوا أن لن يتاب عليهم، فدعاهم الله بهذه الآية.
Qatadah said: It has been mentioned to us that some people had committed grave sins in the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah). When Islam came, they feared that their repentance would not be accepted, so Allah called them with this verse.

وقال ابن عمر: نزلت هذه الآيات في عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد ونفر من المسلمين، كانوا أسلموا ثم فتنوا وعذبوا فافتتنوا فكنا نقول: لا يقبل الله تعالى من هؤلاء صرفا ولا عدلا أبدا، قوم أسلموا ثم تركوا دينهم بعذاب عذبوا به، فنزلت على هؤلاء الآيات فكان عمر بن الخطاب كاتبا فكتبها بيده، ثم بعث بها إلى عياش بن أبي ربيعة والوليد بن الوليد وإلى أولئك النفر فأسلموا وهاجروا.
Ibn ʿUmar said: These verses were revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and a group of Muslims who had embraced Islam, then were tested and tortured, and so they succumbed to the trial. We used to say: "Allah the Exalted will never accept from these people any repentance (ṣarf) or ransom (ʿadl), ever. They are a people who embraced Islam and then abandoned their religion because of the torment they were subjected to." Then these verses were revealed to them. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab was a scribe, so he wrote them with his own hand, then sent them to ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and those men. They embraced Islam and migrated.

أخبرنا أبو عبد الله بن فنجويه حدثنا أبو بكر بن خرجة حدثنا محمّد بن عبد الله بن سلمان الحضرمي حدثنا محمّد بن العلاء حدثنا يونس بن بكير حدثنا ابن إسحاق حدثنا نافع عن ابن عمر عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قال: لما اجتمعنا إلى الهجرة أبعدت أنا وعياش بن أبي ربيعة وهشام بن العاص بن وائل وقلنا: الميعاد بيننا المناصف ميقات بني غفار، فمن حبس منكم لم يأبها فقد حبس فليمض صاحبه، فأصبحت عندها أنا وعياش وحبس عنا هشام وفتن فافتتن، فقدمنا المدينة فكنا نقول: هل يقبل الله من هؤلاء توبة قوم عرفوا الله ورسوله ثم رجعوا عن ذلك لما أصابهم من الدّنيا؟ فأنزل الله تعالى ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوىً لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾.
Abu ʿAbdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Kharjah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-ʿAlaʾ narrated to us: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Nafiʿ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: When we gathered for the migration, I, ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, and Hisham ibn al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il set out, and we said: "Our appointment between us is al-Manasif, the meeting-place of Banu Ghifar. Whoever of you is detained and does not come to it, has been detained; let his companion proceed." So I and ʿAyyash arrived there, but Hisham was detained and was tested, and he succumbed to the trial. We reached Madinah, and we used to say: "Will Allah accept the repentance of people who recognized Allah and His Messenger, then turned back from that because of what worldly affliction befell them?" Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the arrogant?﴾.

قال عمر: فكتبتها بيدي كتابا ثم بعثت بها إلى هشام.
ʿUmar said: I wrote it down with my own hand as a letter, then sent it to Hisham.

قال هشام: فلما قدمت عليّ خرجت بها إلى ذي طوى فقلت اللهم فهمنيها، فعرفت أنها أنزلت فينا، فرجعت فجلست على بعيري فلحقت برسول الله ﷺ.
Hisham said: When it reached me, I went out with it to Dhu Tuwa and said, "O Allah, make me understand it." I then understood that it had been revealed concerning us. So I returned, sat on my camel, and caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Hisham was later martyred at Ajnadayn during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.

وقال بعضهم: نزلت في قوم كانوا يرون أهل الكبائر من أهل النار، فأعلمهم الله تعالى أنه يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً لمن يشاء.
Some of them said: It was revealed concerning a people who used to regard the perpetrators of major sins as people of the Fire, so Allah the Exalted informed them that ﴿He forgives all sins for whomever He wills﴾.

وروى مقاتل بن حيان عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: كنا معشر أصحاب رسول الله نرى أو نقول: أنه ليس شيء من حسناتنا إلّا وهي مقبولة حتّى نزلت هذه الآية ﴿أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَلا تُبْطِلُوا أَعْمالَكُمْ﴾ فلما نزلت هذه الآية قلنا: ما هذا الذي يبطل أعمالنا؟ فقيل لنا:
Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: We, the companions of the Messenger of Allah, used to think, or say, that none of our good deeds would fail to be accepted, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds﴾. When this verse was revealed, we said: "What is this that nullifies our deeds?" It was said to us:
الكبائر والفواحش.
"The major sins and the gross immoralities."

قال: فكنا إذا رأينا من أصاب شيئا منها قلنا: قد هلك، فنزلت هذه الآية، فلما نزلت كففنا عن القول في ذلك، فكنا إذا رأينا أحدا أصاب منها شيئا خفنا عليه، وإن لم يصب منها شيئا رجونا له. وأراد بالإسراف ارتكاب الكبائر، والآية عامة للناس أجمعين لا تَقْنَطُوا.
He said: Whenever we saw someone commit any of them, we said, "He has perished." Then this verse was revealed, and after it was revealed we refrained from speaking about that.
