Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl and al-Akhfash said the meaning of the verse, ﴿And the earth entirely ... and the heavens will be folded up﴾, means: confined and bound, ﴿in His right hand﴾, i.e., by His power, and all of it is in His dominion and His grip, like His saying: ﴿or what your right hands possess﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 36.]], meaning what you had no power over. Dominion does not belong to the right hand to the exclusion of the rest of the body. And Allah knows best.

﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾.

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Mukhallidi informed us, by dictation and reading: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Raja' al-Musisi related to us: Waki' related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Aslam al-ʿIjli, from Bishr ibn Shaghaf, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the Horn.

He said: "It is a horn that is blown into."

[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/162; Sunan al-Darimi: 2/325.]]

﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾, i.e., they die. This is the second blast. They differed about those whom Allah, Exalted, excepted.

Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Rudhbadhi informed us: Abu al-Qasim ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahim al-Shurutì related to us: ʿAbdan ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad related to us: Muhammad ibn Musaffa related to us: Baqiyyah related to us, from Muhammad, from ʿAmr ibn Muhammad, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked Gabriel about this verse, ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾: "Who are those whom Allah did not will to make swoon?"

He said: "They are the martyrs, with their swords hung about them around the Throne."

[[al-Mustadrak: 2/253.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed us by my reading to him: Abu ʿAli ibn Habash the reciter related to us, saying: Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Muthanna al-Mawsili read to me while I was listening: Yahya ibn Ma'in related to us: Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' related to us: Isma'il ibn ʿAyyash related to us, from ʿUmar ibn Muhammad, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): that he asked Gabriel (peace be upon them both) about this verse, ﴿And the Horn will be blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾: "Who are those whom Allah, Exalted, did not will to make swoon?"

He said: "They are the martyrs, with their swords hung about them around His Throne. The angels will meet them on the Day of Resurrection, going to the place of gathering, with camels of ruby whose reins are pearls, with saddles of brocade and silk, whose trappings are softer than silk. The reach of their steps is as far as the reach of men's eyes. They walk in Paradise, and when the time is long, they say: 'Set out to our Lord that we may see how He judges between His creatures.' Then my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will smile upon them, and when He smiles upon a servant in a station, there is no reckoning for him."

[[al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/336.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: al-Hasan ibn Yahyuwayh related to us: ʿAmr ibn Thawr and Ibrahim ibn Abi Sufyan related to us, both saying:
Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firabri related to us: Sulayman ibn Hayyan related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are those whom Allah excepted?"

He said: "They are Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death." He said: "Then He will say: 'O Angel of Death, take the soul of Israfil.' Then He will say: 'O Angel of Death, who remains?' He will say: 'Glory be to You, my Lord, and exalted are You, Possessor of Majesty and Honor; there remain Gabriel, Michael, and the Angel of Death.' Then He will say: 'O Angel of Death, take the soul of Michael.' He takes the soul of Michael, and it falls like a great mountain. Then He will say: 'O Angel of Death, who remains?' He will say: 'Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, Possessor of Majesty and Honor; there remain Gabriel and the Angel of Death.'

Then He will say: 'Die, O Angel of Death,' and he dies. He will say: 'O Gabriel, who remains?' He will say: 'Blessed and exalted are You, Possessor of Majesty and Honor; Your Face remains, Eternal and Everlasting, and Gabriel is dead, perishing.' He said: Then He will say: 'O Gabriel, your death is inevitable,' and he falls prostrate, beating his wings, and says: 'Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, Possessor of Majesty and Honor.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The superiority of His creation over the creation of Michael is like a great mountain over a small hill."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 24/38; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/280.]]

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn Yarham related to us: Muhammad ibn Hammad related to us: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir, regarding His saying: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾, he said: "Moses is among those whom Allah excepted, because he swooned once."

What supports this is what:

ʿAqil ibn Ahmad informed us: that Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi the judge informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Abu Kurayb related to us: ʿAbdah ibn Sulayman related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to us: Abu Salamah related to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A Jew said in the market of Medina: "By Him who chose Moses over mankind." A man from the Ansar raised his hand and slapped his face, saying: "You say this while the Messenger of Allah is among us?"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿And the Horn will be blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾. I will be the first to raise his head, and behold, Moses is holding one of the legs of the Throne, and I do not know whether he raised his head before me or whether he was among those whom Allah excepted."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 24/40.]]

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: they are twelve: the bearers of the Throne, Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death.

Al-Dahhak: they are Ridwan, the houris, Malik, and the Zabaniyah.

Qatadah: Allah knows best their number.

Al-Hasan: "except whom Allah wills" means Allah alone. It was also said: the scorpions and serpents of Hell.

Then it is blown into again, a second time, ﴿and behold, they are standing, looking on﴾, i.e., from their graves, looking toward the resurrection.

It was said: awaiting the command of Allah concerning them.

The scholars said: the purpose of the blowing into the Horn is that it is a sign which Allah made by which the sensible person is alerted and takes heed, and then the renewal of creation.

﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾, i.e., will be illuminated.

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read: (وَأُشْرِقَتِ) in the form of the passive voice, as if it were made radiant.

Most exegetes said: "with the light of its Lord" means with the illumination of its Lord, at the time when the Most Merciful appears to judge between His creatures. They will not be harmed in His light except as one is harmed by the sun on a clear day without haze.

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 24/42.]]

Al-Dahhak said: "with the judgment of its Lord."

Al-Suddi said: "with the justice of its Lord." It is said that Allah creates on the Day of Resurrection a light that covers the face of the earth, so the earth shines by it. It is also said that Allah manifests Himself to the angels, so the earth shines with His light. By "the earth" is meant the plains of the Resurrection.

﴿And the Book will be placed, and the Prophets and the martyrs will be brought forward﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: this means those who bear witness for the messengers that they conveyed the message.

Al-Suddi said: those who were martyred in obedience to Allah.

It was said: they are the guardians (al-Hafazah), supported by His saying: ﴿And every soul will come with it a driver and a witness﴾ [[Surah Qaf: 21.]].

﴿And judgment will be given between them with truth, and they will not be wronged. And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾, violently dragged, dragged on their faces, ﴿in groups﴾, companies one after another, each nation by itself.

Abu ʿUbayd and al-Akhfash said: it means groups in separate divisions; its singular is zumrah.

﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾, its seven gates, which had been closed before that.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 39, verses 65–75 (part 2 of 2):

The readers differed over the words (فُتِحَتْ) and (فُتِّحَتْ). The people of Kufa read them with a light doubling (فُتِحَتْ), while the others read them with a doubled letter (فُتِّحَتْ), indicating multiplicity (al-takthir).

﴿And their keepers will say to them, as a rebuke and reproach: "Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves, reciting to you the signs of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say: "Yes, but the word of punishment has become due against the disbelievers."﴾ Their saying is the word of God Most High: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ [Surah Hud: 119.]

﴿It will be said: "Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever. Evil is the abode of the arrogant."﴾ ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups, (as riders), until, when they reach it and its gates are opened...﴾ The waw in (وَفُتِحَتْ) is the waw of the circumstantial clause (wāw al-ḥāl), and its sense is: "and its gates had been opened." So the waw is introduced here to show that the gates were already open before their arrival, and it is omitted in the first verse to show that the gates of Hell were closed before the arrival of the disbelievers.

It is also said: the waw was added here because the gates of Paradise are eight and the gates of Hell are seven, so the waw was added here to distinguish between them.

Our shaykh 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid related from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdash that it is called the "waw of eight" (wāw al-thamāniya). He said: This is because it is the custom of Quraysh to count numbers from one up to eight, and when they reach eight they add a waw to it, saying: "five, six, seven, and eight." The word of God Most High supports this: ﴿He subjected it against them for seven nights and eight days, in succession﴾ [Surah al-Haqqah: 7], and He, glorified be He, said: ﴿the penitent, the worshippers﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 112], and when He reached the eighth of the attributes He said: ﴿and those who enjoin right and forbid wrong﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 112]. He, glorified and exalted be He, said: ﴿They will say: "They were three, the fourth being their dog," and they say: "They were five, the sixth being their dog," and they say: "They were seven, and the eighth being their dog"﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 22]. And He, Most High, said: ﴿previously married and virgin﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 5].

It is also said: the addition of the waw in describing the Garden is a sign that God's mercy exceeds His wrath and His punishment.

﴿And their keepers will say to them: "Peace be upon you. You are good, so enter it, abiding therein forever."﴾ Qatada said: When they have passed through the Fire, they will be detained at a bridge between the Garden and the Fire, and some of them will take retribution from others. Then, when they have calmed down and become tranquil, Ridwan and his companions will say to them: ﴿"Peace be upon you. You are good, so enter it, abiding therein forever."﴾

Abu Salih Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi informed us: Abu Hatim Makki ibn 'Abdan al-Tamimi informed us: Abu al-Azhar Ahmad ibn al-Azhar al-Sulayti informed us: Rawh ibn 'Ubada al-Qaysi informed us: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn Damra, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): that he was asked about this verse, ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups﴾, the verse.

He said: "They will be led to the gates of Paradise. When they reach them, they will find at its gate a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs flow. They will go to one of them and purify themselves in it, and it will flow over them with the radiance of bliss, so their bodies will never change afterwards, and their hair will never become disheveled afterwards, as if they had been anointed with oil. Then they will go to the other and drink from it, and it will remove whatever is in their bellies of harm or impurity. The angels will meet them at the gates of Paradise: ﴿'Peace be upon you. You are good, so enter it, abiding therein forever.'﴾ Each of them will be met by his young attendants who will go around him, as the young attendants of a man return from his absence (in a journey). They will say: 'Rejoice! God has prepared for you such and such, and has prepared for you such and such.' And one of his young attendants will set off, running to his wives among the wide-eyed houris, and say: 'This is so-and-so, by his name in the world, who has arrived.' They will say: 'Did you see him?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then joy will overwhelm them, until they come out to the threshold of the door. He will come and enter, and behold: ﴿thrones woven together, and cups set out, and cushions arranged in rows, and carpets spread out﴾ [Surah al-Ghashiyah: 13–16]. Then he will look at the foundation of his building, and behold, it is founded upon pearl-dust of various colours: green, red, white, and yellow, of every colour. Then he will recline on one of his couches, then raise his gaze to its ceiling, and were it not that God had decreed it for him, his sight would have been nearly taken away, for it is like lightning. He will say: ﴿'Praise be to God, who guided us to this. We would never have been guided had God not guided us'﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 43]." He said: "Then the angels will call to them: ﴿'That is the Garden, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.'﴾"

The grammarians differed over the answer (jawāb) to the phrase ﴿until, when they reach it﴾ (ḥattā idhā jā'ūhā).

Some of them said: its answer is (فُتِحَتْ), and the waw in it is [affirmed], its sense being: "until, when they reach it, its gates have been opened," like the word of God Most High: ﴿And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya': 48], meaning "a light."

It is also said: its answer is the word of God Most High: ﴿and its keepers will say to them﴾, and the waw in it is redundant (mulghāh), its estimated sense being: "until, when they reach it, and its gates have been opened, and its keepers say to them..."

Like the saying of the poet:
"Then, that, O Kabisha, was not ... except a dreamer's illusion in a phantom."
[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 24/46. In al-Lisan: 2/551, it is attributed to Ibn Muqbil, and in it:
"Then, that, O Kabisha, was not ... except the word of a dreamer in a phantom."]
He meant: "Then that was not."

Some of them said: its answer is elided, and the meaning of the statement is: ﴿until, when they reach it, and its gates have been opened, and its keepers say to them: "Peace be upon you. You are good, so enter it, abiding therein forever"﴾, so they entered it.

﴿And they will say: "Praise be to God..."﴾ Abu 'Ubayda said: its answer is elided and its predicate is omitted, and the Arabs do this when the context indicates it.

Al-Akhtal said at the end of one of his odes:
"Except that the tribe of Quraysh excelled ... over the people, or the nobles of Nahshal."
[Tafsir al-Tabari: 24/47; Sharh al-Radi 'ala al-Kafiya: 4/377.]

And 'Abd Manaf ibn Rabi' said at the end of an ode:
"Until, when they drive them into a stony land, lame, as a herd of camels is driven, scattered."
[Ibid.; and Lisan al-'Arab: 3/237.]

﴿And they will say: "Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has made us inherit the land,"﴾ meaning the land of Paradise. This is the word of God Most High: ﴿And We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya': 105].

﴿We will dwell in the Garden wherever we wish. How excellent is the reward of those who work.﴾ The reward of the obedient. ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praise of their Lord﴾: encircling, surrounding, enclosing it on all sides. The particle (min) in (مِنْ حَوْلِ) is for emphasis. ﴿glorifying with the praise of their Lord﴾: taking delight in that, not worshipping through it, because the obligation (taklif) will cease on that Day. ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth﴾, meaning between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, with truth. ﴿And it will be said: "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds."﴾

Abu Salih Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi al-Faqih informed us: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us: Abu al-Azhar Ahmad ibn al-Azhar informed us: Rawh ibn 'Ubada informed us: Sa'id informed us, from Qatada, concerning this verse, he said: "The first of creation was opened with praise, when He said: ﴿Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 1], and it was concluded with praise, when He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth. And it will be said: 'Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.'﴾"

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik informed us: Abu Talha Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Karim al-Fazari informed us: Nasr ibn 'Ali informed us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman informed us, from 'Ubada ibn Maysara, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited on the pulpit the end of Surah al-Zumar, and the pulpit shook twice.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 39, verse 65–75 (part 1 of 2):

Indeed it has been revealed to you and to those before you: ﴿If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers.﴾ That is, if you associate partners with Allah, the deeds you did before the association will be nullified.

The people of allusion (ahl al-Ishara) said: its meaning is, "If you look at other than Me in secret, your deeds will surely be nullified."

Then He directed him to monotheism, so He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone, and be among the thankful﴾, thankful to Allah Most High for the blessing of faith. ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾, when they associated others with Him. Then He informed of His greatness, saying: ﴿And the earth entirely will be His handful﴾, meaning His dominion on the Day of Resurrection, without any hindrance, rival, or claimant. Today too it is His dominion. Its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [[Surah al-Fatihah: 4.]] and ﴿To whom belongs the dominion today?﴾ [[Surah Ghafir: 16.]]

Al-Akhfash said: this is like saying "Khurasan is in the grip of so-and-so," not that it is in his palm, but its meaning is that it is under his dominion.

﴿And the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾. Folding (tayy) has several meanings: gathering up, as one folds a sheet of paper or a garment, as in His saying: ﴿The Day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾. From it also comes concealment, as you say: "I hid so-and-so from the eyes," and "Conceal this statement from me," i.e., keep it secret.

From it also comes turning away: one says, "I folded myself away from so-and-so," or "I turned away from him."

From it also comes annihilation: the Arabs say, "I folded so-and-so with my sword," meaning I destroyed him.

The common reading is مَطْوِيَّاتٌ with a nominative ending (raf'). ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it with a kasra (bi-l-kasr). Its position is accusative (nasb) as a circumstantial (ḥāl) and as a detached clause (qaṭʿ). The mention of the right hand is for emphasis on power.

It was said: it means strength, as in the poet's words:
*"ʿArābah met her with the right hand"* [[al-Sihah: 1/180; Lisan al-ʿArab: 1/593; it is by al-Shammakh.]]

It was also said: "yamin" here means an oath, because He swore that He would fold them and annihilate them. This is the view chosen by ʿAlī ibn Mahdī al-Ṭabarī, who said: its meaning is "wearied by His oath."

Our teacher Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib related this to me from him.

Then He declared Himself free of imperfection, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate.﴾

Then he mentioned some of the reports transmitted concerning the interpretation of this verse.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, by my reading to him: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Mutari related to us: ʿAlī ibn Ḥarb al-Mawṣilī related to us: Ibn Fuḍayl related to us: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, indeed Allah holds the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the mountains on one finger, the trees on one finger, and the creatures on one finger, then He says, 'Thus,' with His hand."

The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed, then he said: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾.

[[Musnad Ahmad: 1/429; Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/49, no. 3291, with slight variation.]]

And ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed me: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Faqih informed us: al-ʿAbbas ibn al-Fadl al-Asqati related to us: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us: Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyad related to us, from Manṣur, from Ibrahim, from ʿUbaydah, from ʿUbayd Allah, who said: A rabbi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, or O Abu al-Qasim, indeed Allah holds the heavens on the Day of Resurrection on one finger, the earths on one finger, the mountains on one finger, the trees on one finger, the dust on one finger, and the rest of creation on one finger; He shakes them and says: 'I am the King, I am the King.'"

The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed in wonder at what the rabbi said, confirming him, then he recited: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, and the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

[[Sahih Muslim: 8/125.]]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Qasri informed us there: Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us in Baghdad: al-Hasan ibn ʿArafah related to us: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Wasiti related to us, from Sulayman ibn Muhammad, from ʿUmar ibn Nafiʿ, from his father, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing on this pulpit — meaning the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) — and he was relating from his Lord, blessed and exalted, and he said: 'When it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Exalted, will gather the seven heavens and earths into His handful' — then he said, 'Thus,' and tightened His grip, then opened it — 'then He says: I am Allah, I am the Merciful, I am the King, I am the Holy, I am the Peace, I am the Giver of Security, I am the Guardian, I am the Mighty, I am the Compeller, I am the Proud, I am the One who began the world when it was nothing, I am the One who will restore it. Where are the kings? Where are the tyrants?'"

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Fadl related to us: Hudbah ibn Khalid related to us: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from Ishaq ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Miqsam, from Ibn ʿUmar: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited on the pulpit: (﻿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, and the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand). Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) extended his hands and said: "Then Allah glorifies Himself: I am the Compeller, I am the Proud, I am the Mighty, I am the King. Where are the compellers? Where are the proud?"

He said: the pulpit trembled until we said, "It will surely move with him," and it was said, "It will surely fall with him."

[[Kitab al-Sunnah of Ibn Abi ʿAsim: 241, no. 545.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us: ʿUmar related to us, from ʿAbd Allah: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah related to us: Abu Usamah related to us, from ʿUmar ibn Hamzah, from Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar related to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Allah will fold up the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, then take them in His right hand, then say: I am the King. Where are the compellers? Where are the proud?"

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 24/36.]]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us by license: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'unah informed us: Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' related to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam al-Ghassani related to us, from Saʿid ibn Thawban al-Kalaʿi, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, from the Prophet (ﷺ): that a rabbi from the rabbis of the Jews came to him and said: "I will ask you about some things, so inform me of them."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Ask that."

The rabbi said: "Tell me about the saying of Allah in His Book: ﴿The Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens﴾. Where are the creatures at that time?"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They are the guests of Allah, Exalted, so what He has will not fail them."

The rabbi said: "Then, the saying of Allah, Glory be to Him and Exalted: ﴿And the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾. Where are the creatures at that time?"

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They will be in it like the inscribed tablet in the book."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/333.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: in this verse, all of it is His right hand, and there is nothing in His other hand; He only uses His left hand, which is occupied by His right. And the seven heavens and earths in the hand of Allah, Exalted, are only like a mustard seed in the hand of one of you.

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 24/32.]]

ʿAqil ibn Ahmad informed me: that al-Muʿafa ibn Zakariyya informed him, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Ibn Humayd related to us: Salamah related to us: Ibn Ishaq related to me, from Muhammad, from Saʿid, who said: A group of Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said:
"O Muhammad, this is Allah who created the creatures, so who created Him?"

The Prophet (ﷺ) became angry until his color changed, then he rushed at them in anger for his Lord. Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and calmed him, and said: "Lower your wing," and there came to him from Allah the answer to what they asked, saying: Allah says: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.﴾

When the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it to them, they said: "Describe your Lord to us: how He created, how His arm is, how His forearm is?"

The Prophet (ﷺ) became angrier than his first anger, then he rushed at them, and Gabriel came and said the like of his speech, and brought him the answer to what they asked: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, and the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾, etc.

[[Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/410.]]

Mujahid said: "Both hands of the Most Merciful are right hands."

Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isbahani informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq informed us: Bishr ibn Musa related to us: al-Humaydi related to us: Sufyan related to us: ʿAmr ibn Dinar informed us: ʿAmr ibn Aws al-Thaqafi informed us:
that he heard ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The just ones with Allah on the Day of Resurrection will be upon pulpits of light, at the right hand of the Most Merciful, and both His hands are right hands — those who act justly in their judgment, their families, and what they are charged with."

[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/160; al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi: 10/87.]]

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl and al-Akhfash said the meaning of the verse, ﴿And the earth entirely ... and the heavens will be folded up﴾, means: confined and bound, ﴿in His right hand﴾, i.e., by His power, and all of it is in His dominion and His grip, like His saying: ﴿or what your right hands possess﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 36.]], meaning what you had no power over. Dominion does not belong to the right hand to the exclusion of the rest of the body. And Allah knows best.

﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾.

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Mukhallidi informed us, by dictation and reading: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Raja' al-Musisi related to us: Waki' related to us: Sufyan related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Aslam al-ʿIjli, from Bishr ibn Shaghaf, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the Horn.

He said: "It is a horn that is blown into."

[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/162; Sunan al-Darimi: 2/325.]]

﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾, i.e., they die. This is the second blast. They differed about those whom Allah, Exalted, excepted.

Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Rudhbadhi informed us: Abu al-Qasim ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahim al-Shurutì related to us: ʿAbdan ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad related to us: Muhammad ibn Musaffa related to us: Baqiyyah related to us, from Muhammad, from ʿAmr ibn Muhammad, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked Gabriel about this verse, ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾: "Who are those whom Allah did not will to make swoon?"

He said: "They are the martyrs, with their swords hung about them around the Throne."

[[al-Mustadrak: 2/253.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed us by my reading to him: Abu ʿAli ibn Habash the reciter related to us, saying: Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Muthanna al-Mawsili read to me while I was listening: Yahya ibn Ma'in related to us: Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' related to us: Isma'il ibn ʿAyyash related to us, from ʿUmar ibn Muhammad, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): that he asked Gabriel (peace be upon them both) about this verse, ﴿And the Horn will be blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾: "Who are those whom Allah, Exalted, did not will to make swoon?"

He said: "They are the martyrs, with their swords hung about them around His Throne. The angels will meet them on the Day of Resurrection, going to the place of gathering, with camels of ruby whose reins are pearls, with saddles of brocade and silk, whose trappings are softer than silk. The reach of their steps is as far as the reach of men's eyes. They walk in Paradise, and when the time is long, they say: 'Set out to our Lord that we may see how He judges between His creatures.' Then my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will smile upon them, and when He smiles upon a servant in a station, there is no reckoning for him."

[[al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/336.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: al-Hasan ibn Yahyuwayh related to us: ʿAmr ibn Thawr and Ibrahim ibn Abi Sufyan related to us, both saying:
Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firabri related to us: Sulayman ibn Hayyan related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are those whom Allah excepted?"

He said: "They are Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death." He said: "Then He will say: 'O Angel of Death, take the soul of Israfil.' Then He will say: 'O Angel of Death, who remains?' He will say: 'Glory be to You, my Lord, and exalted are You, Possessor of Majesty and Honor; there remain Gabriel, Michael, and the Angel of Death.' Then He will say: 'O Angel of Death, take the soul of Michael.' He takes the soul of Michael, and it falls like a great mountain. Then He will say: 'O Angel of Death, who remains?' He will say: 'Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, Possessor of Majesty and Honor; there remain Gabriel and the Angel of Death.'

Then He will say: 'Die, O Angel of Death,' and he dies. He will say: 'O Gabriel, who remains?' He will say: 'Blessed and exalted are You, Possessor of Majesty and Honor; Your Face remains, Eternal and Everlasting, and Gabriel is dead, perishing.' He said: Then He will say: 'O Gabriel, your death is inevitable,' and he falls prostrate, beating his wings, and says: 'Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, Possessor of Majesty and Honor.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The superiority of His creation over the creation of Michael is like a great mountain over a small hill."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 24/38; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/280.]]

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn Yarham related to us: Muhammad ibn Hammad related to us: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir, regarding His saying: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾, he said: "Moses is among those whom Allah excepted, because he swooned once."

What supports this is what:

ʿAqil ibn Ahmad informed us: that Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi the judge informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Abu Kurayb related to us: ʿAbdah ibn Sulayman related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to us: Abu Salamah related to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A Jew said in the market of Medina: "By Him who chose Moses over mankind." A man from the Ansar raised his hand and slapped his face, saying: "You say this while the Messenger of Allah is among us?"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿And the Horn will be blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾. I will be the first to raise his head, and behold, Moses is holding one of the legs of the Throne, and I do not know whether he raised his head before me or whether he was among those whom Allah excepted."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 24/40.]]

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: they are twelve: the bearers of the Throne, Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death.

Al-Dahhak: they are Ridwan, the houris, Malik, and the Zabaniyah.

Qatadah: Allah knows best their number.

Al-Hasan: "except whom Allah wills" means Allah alone. It was also said: the scorpions and serpents of Hell.

Then it is blown into again, a second time, ﴿and behold, they are standing, looking on﴾, i.e., from their graves, looking toward the resurrection.

It was said: awaiting the command of Allah concerning them.

The scholars said: the purpose of the blowing into the Horn is that it is a sign which Allah made by which the sensible person is alerted and takes heed, and then the renewal of creation.

﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾, i.e., will be illuminated.

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read: (وَأُشْرِقَتِ) in the form of the passive voice, as if it were made radiant.

Most exegetes said: "with the light of its Lord" means with the illumination of its Lord, at the time when the Most Merciful appears to judge between His creatures. They will not be harmed in His light except as one is harmed by the sun on a clear day without haze.

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 24/42.]]

Al-Dahhak said: "with the judgment of its Lord."

Al-Suddi said: "with the justice of its Lord." It is said that Allah creates on the Day of Resurrection a light that covers the face of the earth, so the earth shines by it. It is also said that Allah manifests Himself to the angels, so the earth shines with His light. By "the earth" is meant the plains of the Resurrection.

﴿And the Book will be placed, and the Prophets and the martyrs will be brought forward﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: this means those who bear witness for the messengers that they conveyed the message.

Al-Suddi said: those who were martyred in obedience to Allah.

It was said: they are the guardians (al-Hafazah), supported by His saying: ﴿And every soul will come with it a driver and a witness﴾ [[Surah Qaf: 21.]].

﴿And judgment will be given between them with truth, and they will not be wronged. And every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾, violently dragged, dragged on their faces, ﴿in groups﴾, companies one after another, each nation by itself.

Abu ʿUbayd and al-Akhfash said: it means groups in separate divisions; its singular is zumrah.

﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾, its seven gates, which had been closed before that.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 39, verses 65–75 (part 2 of 2):

The readers differed over the words (فُتِحَتْ) and (فُتِّحَتْ). The people of Kufa read them with a light doubling (فُتِحَتْ), while the others read them with a doubled letter (فُتِّحَتْ), indicating multiplicity (al-takthir).

﴿And their keepers will say to them, as a rebuke and reproach: "Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves, reciting to you the signs of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say: "Yes, but the word of punishment has become due against the disbelievers."﴾ Their saying is the word of God Most High: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ [Surah Hud: 119.]

﴿It will be said: "Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever. Evil is the abode of the arrogant."﴾ ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups, (as riders), until, when they reach it and its gates are opened...﴾ The waw in (وَفُتِحَتْ) is the waw of the circumstantial clause (wāw al-ḥāl), and its sense is: "and its gates had been opened." So the waw is introduced here to show that the gates were already open before their arrival, and it is omitted in the first verse to show that the gates of Hell were closed before the arrival of the disbelievers.

It is also said: the waw was added here because the gates of Paradise are eight and the gates of Hell are seven, so the waw was added here to distinguish between them.

Our shaykh 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid related from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdash that it is called the "waw of eight" (wāw al-thamāniya). He said: This is because it is the custom of Quraysh to count numbers from one up to eight, and when they reach eight they add a waw to it, saying: "five, six, seven, and eight." The word of God Most High supports this: ﴿He subjected it against them for seven nights and eight days, in succession﴾ [Surah al-Haqqah: 7], and He, glorified be He, said: ﴿the penitent, the worshippers﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 112], and when He reached the eighth of the attributes He said: ﴿and those who enjoin right and forbid wrong﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 112]. He, glorified and exalted be He, said: ﴿They will say: "They were three, the fourth being their dog," and they say: "They were five, the sixth being their dog," and they say: "They were seven, and the eighth being their dog"﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 22]. And He, Most High, said: ﴿previously married and virgin﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 5].

It is also said: the addition of the waw in describing the Garden is a sign that God's mercy exceeds His wrath and His punishment.

﴿And their keepers will say to them: "Peace be upon you. You are good, so enter it, abiding therein forever."﴾ Qatada said: When they have passed through the Fire, they will be detained at a bridge between the Garden and the Fire, and some of them will take retribution from others. Then, when they have calmed down and become tranquil, Ridwan and his companions will say to them: ﴿"Peace be upon you. You are good, so enter it, abiding therein forever."﴾

Abu Salih Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi informed us: Abu Hatim Makki ibn 'Abdan al-Tamimi informed us: Abu al-Azhar Ahmad ibn al-Azhar al-Sulayti informed us: Rawh ibn 'Ubada al-Qaysi informed us: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn Damra, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): that he was asked about this verse, ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups﴾, the verse.

He said: "They will be led to the gates of Paradise. When they reach them, they will find at its gate a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs flow. They will go to one of them and purify themselves in it, and it will flow over them with the radiance of bliss, so their bodies will never change afterwards, and their hair will never become disheveled afterwards, as if they had been anointed with oil. Then they will go to the other and drink from it, and it will remove whatever is in their bellies of harm or impurity. The angels will meet them at the gates of Paradise: ﴿'Peace be upon you. You are good, so enter it, abiding therein forever.'﴾ Each of them will be met by his young attendants who will go around him, as the young attendants of a man return from his absence (in a journey). They will say: 'Rejoice! God has prepared for you such and such, and has prepared for you such and such.' And one of his young attendants will set off, running to his wives among the wide-eyed houris, and say: 'This is so-and-so, by his name in the world, who has arrived.' They will say: 'Did you see him?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then joy will overwhelm them, until they come out to the threshold of the door. He will come and enter, and behold: ﴿thrones woven together, and cups set out, and cushions arranged in rows, and carpets spread out﴾ [Surah al-Ghashiyah: 13–16]. Then he will look at the foundation of his building, and behold, it is founded upon pearl-dust of various colours: green, red, white, and yellow, of every colour. Then he will recline on one of his couches, then raise his gaze to its ceiling, and were it not that God had decreed it for him, his sight would have been nearly taken away, for it is like lightning. He will say: ﴿'Praise be to God, who guided us to this. We would never have been guided had God not guided us'﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 43]." He said: "Then the angels will call to them: ﴿'That is the Garden, which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.'﴾"

The grammarians differed over the answer (jawāb) to the phrase ﴿until, when they reach it﴾ (ḥattā idhā jā'ūhā).

Some of them said: its answer is (فُتِحَتْ), and the waw in it is [affirmed], its sense being: "until, when they reach it, its gates have been opened," like the word of God Most High: ﴿And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya': 48], meaning "a light."

It is also said: its answer is the word of God Most High: ﴿and its keepers will say to them﴾, and the waw in it is redundant (mulghāh), its estimated sense being: "until, when they reach it, and its gates have been opened, and its keepers say to them..."

Like the saying of the poet:
"Then, that, O Kabisha, was not ... except a dreamer's illusion in a phantom."
[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 24/46. In al-Lisan: 2/551, it is attributed to Ibn Muqbil, and in it:
"Then, that, O Kabisha, was not ... except the word of a dreamer in a phantom."]
He meant: "Then that was not."

Some of them said: its answer is elided, and the meaning of the statement is: ﴿until, when they reach it, and its gates have been opened, and its keepers say to them: "Peace be upon you. You are good, so enter it, abiding therein forever"﴾, so they entered it.

﴿And they will say: "Praise be to God..."﴾ Abu 'Ubayda said: its answer is elided and its predicate is omitted, and the Arabs do this when the context indicates it.

Al-Akhtal said at the end of one of his odes:
"Except that the tribe of Quraysh excelled ... over the people, or the nobles of Nahshal."
[Tafsir al-Tabari: 24/47; Sharh al-Radi 'ala al-Kafiya: 4/377.]

And 'Abd Manaf ibn Rabi' said at the end of an ode:
"Until, when they drive them into a stony land, lame, as a herd of camels is driven, scattered."
[Ibid.; and Lisan al-'Arab: 3/237.]

﴿And they will say: "Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has made us inherit the land,"﴾ meaning the land of Paradise. This is the word of God Most High: ﴿And We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya': 105].

﴿We will dwell in the Garden wherever we wish. How excellent is the reward of those who work.﴾ The reward of the obedient. ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praise of their Lord﴾: encircling, surrounding, enclosing it on all sides. The particle (min) in (مِنْ حَوْلِ) is for emphasis. ﴿glorifying with the praise of their Lord﴾: taking delight in that, not worshipping through it, because the obligation (taklif) will cease on that Day. ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth﴾, meaning between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, with truth. ﴿And it will be said: "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds."﴾

Abu Salih Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad al-Bayhaqi al-Faqih informed us: Makki ibn 'Abdan informed us: Abu al-Azhar Ahmad ibn al-Azhar informed us: Rawh ibn 'Ubada informed us: Sa'id informed us, from Qatada, concerning this verse, he said: "The first of creation was opened with praise, when He said: ﴿Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 1], and it was concluded with praise, when He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth. And it will be said: 'Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.'﴾"

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik informed us: Abu Talha Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Karim al-Fazari informed us: Nasr ibn 'Ali informed us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman informed us, from 'Ubada ibn Maysara, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited on the pulpit the end of Surah al-Zumar, and the pulpit shook twice.
